# Budgetum Help Center

Source: https://budgetum.app/help

Budgetum is an offline budget planner and expense tracker for iPhone and Android. This file contains every Help Center guide as Markdown.

## Key Concepts

Budgetum is built from a few building blocks. Only categories and transactions are required; everything else is optional.

- **Budget:** your plan for a calendar month or a saved [custom budget period](https://budgetum.app/help/custom-budget-periods) (for example payday to payday), compared with what actually happened. See [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget).
- **Sections:** groups of categories, for example Housing, Food, or Income.
- **Categories:** what each income or expense belongs to. Every regular income or expense transaction has exactly one category. Sections and categories are one shared list used by every month; plans are separate for each month or period. See [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories).
- **Transactions:** income and expense records. They count toward your budget. See [Add and edit transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction).
- **Accounts:** where money is kept, such as bank, cash, card, savings, or debt. An account can use a currency different from your main (budget) currency. See [Accounts](https://budgetum.app/help/accounts).
- **Transfers:** moving money between your accounts. A transfer is not spending.
- **Balance adjustments:** manual corrections to an account balance. They are not spending either.
- **Contacts:** the stores, services, and people you pay or get paid by. See [Contacts](https://budgetum.app/help/contacts).
- **Tags:** optional labels that cross categories, such as a trip or a project. A transaction can have several tags, and a tag can be on many transactions. See [Tags](https://budgetum.app/help/tags).
- **Receipts:** one purchase split into several transactions, each with its own category. Receipts use accounts in your main currency. See [Receipts](https://budgetum.app/help/receipts).
- **Recurring transactions and favourites:** saved transaction templates. A template can be a favourite, have a repeat schedule, or both. Only active schedules create upcoming transactions, which you confirm. Favourites are added manually: long-press **+** on Budget or Transactions and pick one. See [Recurring transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring).
- **Saved Sets (Pro):** saved include/exclude filters for reviewing matching transactions, opening their analytics, or changing them in bulk. Sets can also be shown on the Budget screen with their own plans. See [Saved Sets](https://budgetum.app/help/saved-sets).
- **Bank statement matching (Pro):** import a CSV or XLSX bank statement for one account and match its rows to your transactions. In the app it is called **Match bank statement**. See [Bank statement matching](https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching).
- **Import / Export:** CSV export and import, plus an optional analytics ZIP for Desktop Analytics. See [Settings](https://budgetum.app/help/settings#import--export).
- **Desktop Analytics:** private reports on a computer at budgetum.app/analytics. Your export is read in the browser, not uploaded.
- **Free and Pro:** core budgeting is free. Free allows up to **5 tags** and **5 recurring templates**. Budgetum Pro is a one-time purchase that removes those limits and unlocks Saved Sets and bank statement matching.

## Rules That Apply Everywhere

- Budgetum is flexible and does not force a budgeting method. See [Budgetum philosophy](https://budgetum.app/help/philosophy).
- Transfers and balance adjustments change account balances only. They never count as budget income or spending, and Analytics leaves them out.
- Analytics uses saved transactions in the selected date range; upcoming recurring previews are not included. Changing the dates keeps your whole drill-down selection.
- Refunds: the Analytics summary shows gross expenses and income, with refunds counted in received income. Expense breakdowns show net amounts after refunds. For example, a $100 purchase and a $20 refund in the same category show as $80 in the breakdown.
- Tags in Analytics: a transaction with several tags is divided equally between them, refunds included. A $100 expense tagged A and B counts $50 toward each tag, so a tag's amount in a breakdown can differ from the total of its full transaction list. See [Analytics and reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics#refunds-and-tag-allocation).
- Foreign-currency accounts: budget totals use the transaction's budget amount in your main currency, while the account balance uses the amount in the account's own currency.
- Scheduled recurring transactions can require confirmation. While any are waiting, the **Transactions** tab shows a small `?` badge.
- Make a backup before importing a CSV. Re-importing a Budgetum export skips transactions that already exist (matched by their ID).
- Contact and tag fields on the Add Transaction form can be hidden with **Show on transaction creation** in the Contacts and Tags screen settings.

## First Run
- **Onboarding** - First-launch setup: welcome, language and currency, suggested categories or start from scratch, optional category selection and planned amounts → see [Onboarding](https://budgetum.app/help#onboarding) below

## Main Navigation
- **Home/Budget** - Main dashboard showing budget overview, spending progress, category summaries, and (when **Quick plan update** is on) quick planned-amount edits → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)
- **Transactions** - List of budget income and expense transactions for the selected period. When some scheduled transactions still need confirmation, the tab shows a small `?` badge → [Transactions screen](https://budgetum.app/help/transactions)
- **Accounts** - Manage account groups, balances, transfers, statement import, and account-specific history → [Accounts](https://budgetum.app/help/accounts)
- **More** - App preferences and configuration (appearance, backup, import/export, categories, contacts, tags, recurring, saved sets, help, quick tips, about, official links, and extras). A small dot can appear on this tab when Budgetum has a rate-the-app prompt ready → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)

## Budget Management
- **Custom Budget Periods** - Create and manage non-monthly budget ranges, such as pay cycles or project budgets. When the selected period ends, Budget asks once whether to move its dates or create the next period with the same plan → [Custom budget periods](https://budgetum.app/help/custom-budget-periods)
- **Budget Settings** - Configure Budget screen display, summary behavior, and budget-calculation preferences → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)
- **Reorder Budget** - Change the display order of sections and categories within the current budget → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)
- **Budget Sync / Copy Plan** - Import selected category plans from another month or custom period into the current period. Categories that already exist in the current period are skipped. When a new month starts, Budget can offer to copy last month's plan once → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)
- **Budget PDF Export** - Configure export settings, export the selected month or custom budget period as a PDF, or generate a link to a web copy of the budget plan → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)
- **Budget Trends** - Per-category or per-section history screen showing monthly planned vs actual amounts for a selected year, with a chart and month-by-month drill-down. Opened from the history icon on a category or section in the Budget or Categories screens → [Budget screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget)

## Categories & Sections
- **Categories Overview** - Master list of all sections and categories, available from **More -> Advanced Features -> Categories**. Categories can also be created directly from the Budget screen → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Add Category** - Create a new category within a section → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Edit Category** - Modify a category's name, icon, color, or section → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Category Details** - Detailed view of a specific category with its transactions → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Merge Categories** - Combine categories, add plans within each month/custom period, and update transactions, templates, Saved Sets, import rules, and hidden notes → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Add Section** - Create a new section to group categories → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Edit Section** - Modify a section's name, icon, or color → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Reorder Categories / Sections** - Change display order of categories and sections → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)
- **Archived Categories** - View hidden/archived categories → [Categories and sections](https://budgetum.app/help/categories)

## Transactions
- **Add Transaction** - Record a new income or expense → [Add and edit transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction)
- **Edit Transaction** - Modify an existing transaction → [Add and edit transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction)
- **Daily Transactions** - View transactions for a specific day with calendar navigation → [Day view](https://budgetum.app/help/day-view)
- **Transaction Search** - Search and filter transactions
- **Transaction History** - View transaction change history
- **Grouped Transactions** - View transactions grouped by various criteria
- **Entity Transactions** - View all transactions for a specific account, category, section, contact, or tag → [Transactions for an account, category, contact, or tag](https://budgetum.app/help/entity-transactions)
- **Saved Sets** - Save reusable transaction conditions for analysis and bulk updates → [Saved Sets](https://budgetum.app/help/saved-sets)

## Receipts
- **Add Receipt** - Capture and record a receipt → [Receipts](https://budgetum.app/help/receipts)
- **Add Receipt Item** - Add individual items from a receipt → [Receipts](https://budgetum.app/help/receipts)
- **Receipt History** - View past receipts → [Receipts](https://budgetum.app/help/receipts)

## Accounts
- **Accounts Overview** - List of all financial accounts (bank, cash, cards, etc.) → [Accounts](https://budgetum.app/help/accounts)
- **Account Flow Chart** - Account-specific inflow, outflow, and balance trends from the account menu → [Accounts](https://budgetum.app/help/accounts)
- **Account Goals** - Set a target balance on an account and track progress in the account list → [Accounts](https://budgetum.app/help/accounts)
- **Add Account** - Create a new financial account
- **Edit Account** - Modify account details
- **Statement Import** - Import a bank statement for one account and match rows to existing transactions → [Bank statement matching](https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching)
- **Add Balance** - Record a balance adjustment
- **Edit Balance** - Modify a balance entry
- **Transfer Between Accounts** - Move money between accounts
- **Edit Transfer** - Modify a transfer
- **Reorder Accounts** - Change account display order
- **Archived Accounts** - View hidden/archived accounts
- **Account Groups** - Organize accounts into groups

## Tags
- **Tags Overview** - List of all transaction tags → [Tags](https://budgetum.app/help/tags)
- **Add Tag** - Create a new tag
- **Edit Tag** - Modify a tag
- **Tag Settings** - Configure tag preferences
- **Merge Tags** - Combine existing tags into an active target, updating transactions, favourites, recurring entries, and Saved Sets → [Tags](https://budgetum.app/help/tags)
- **Archived Tags** - View hidden/archived tags

## Recurring Transactions
- **Recurring Overview** - Saved templates for schedules and manual reuse; Favourites is the first filter and opens by default when any favourites exist. Drag favourites to save their order → [Recurring transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring)
- **Edit Recurring Template** - Modify a recurring transaction template
- **Recurring Options** - Mark Favourite independently of the repeat schedule. Turning it on keeps options open; choosing a repeat option returns with both choices. Save the parent form to keep changes. Favourite-only templates share the existing template Pro limits.
- **Custom Recurring** - Create custom recurring schedules

## Contacts
- **Contacts Overview** - List of people/businesses you transact with → [Contacts](https://budgetum.app/help/contacts)
- **Add Contact** - Create a new contact
- **Edit Contact** - Modify contact details
- **Contact Settings** - Configure contact preferences
- **Merge Contacts** - Combine existing contacts into an active target, updating transactions, favourites, recurring entries, and Saved Sets → [Contacts](https://budgetum.app/help/contacts)
- **Archived Contacts** - View hidden/archived contacts

## Analytics
- **Analytics & Reports** - In-app charts and insights about spending patterns, trends, period comparison, and financial health → [Analytics and reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics)
- **Analytics drill-down** - Each selection keeps the earlier filters, including the starting set or entity. Compact breadcrumbs below the summary return to earlier levels; the title shows the current entity.
- **Transactions in analytics** - The last option in the breakdown selector. It opens automatically when no useful breakdown remains, uses receipt/contact groups, and shows about 100 transactions at a time without splitting groups. Totals cover all matches.
- **Spending calendar** - Full-year daily spending (or income) heatmap from Analytics → More analytics → [Analytics and reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics)
- **Desktop Analytics** - Browser-based private reports at budgetum.app/analytics, fed by an Import / Export CSV or analytics ZIP → [Analytics and reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics) and [Settings](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)

## Data Management
- **Backup / Restore** - Create a backup file of all your data or restore from a previous backup → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)
- **Import / Export** - Export transactions as CSV or a desktop-analytics ZIP; import Budgetum CSV, YNAB Register.csv, or other CSVs with column mapping → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)

## Shared Components
- **Shared UI Components** - Common interface elements used throughout the app (Date Picker, Number Picker, Period Picker, Summary Card, Bottom Sheets, and more) → [Date picker, calculator, and other shared controls](https://budgetum.app/help/shared-components)

## Product Foundations
- **Budgetum Philosophy** - Product principles and budgeting stance → [Budgetum philosophy](https://budgetum.app/help/philosophy)

## Other
- **Budgetum Pro / Upgrade** - One-time purchase that unlocks Pro features (Saved Sets, bank statement matching, and more than 5 tags / recurring templates). Managed from the top of the More screen → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)
- **Say thanks** - Optional one-time tips to the developer on iOS and Android. Open More → About → Say thanks; tips do not unlock Pro features → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)
- **Appearance** - Theme mode (light/dark/system) and primary color → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)
- **Localization** - Language, currency, number format, and privacy options (hide currency symbol, hide numbers) → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)
- **Tips & Assistance** - Reset tutorial hints, open the Budgetum Assistant, and watch quick video tips → [Settings, backup, and import / export](https://budgetum.app/help/settings)

## Onboarding

Onboarding runs the first time you open Budgetum after install (until you complete it). It sets language and currency, optionally seeds categories and planned amounts, then takes you to the Budget screen.

### When it appears

- Shown when onboarding has not been completed
- After completion, the app opens on the normal Budget screen; onboarding does not repeat unless you reset the app data or reinstall

### Steps

### 1. Welcome

Introduces Budgetum and what you will set up next. Continue to move forward.

### 2. Localization

Choose:
- **Language** — app UI language
- **Currency** — default currency for amounts and formatting

These match what you can change later under **More → Localization**.

### 3. Setup choice

Pick how to build your first budget:

- **Use suggested categories** — continue to pick from Budgetum’s starter category list and optional planned amounts
- **Start from scratch** — skip category seeding; you add sections and categories yourself on the Budget screen after onboarding

### 4. Category selection (suggested path only)

If you chose suggested categories:
- Browse starter categories grouped by section
- Select the ones you want in your budget
- Continue when you have at least one selected, or go back to change the setup choice

If you started from scratch, this step is skipped.

### 5. Planned amounts (suggested path, with selections)

If you selected categories:
- Set a planned amount for each selected category (Number Picker)
- You can adjust plans later on the Budget screen

If you selected categories but skip amounts, you can still finish; plans can be added later.

### Navigation

- **Back** — previous step when available
- **Continue / Finish** — advance; on the last step, completes onboarding and loads the Budget screen

The progress indicator reflects how many steps apply (scratch setup has fewer steps than the full suggested flow).

### What gets created

**Suggested categories path:**
- Selected starter categories (and their sections) are created in your database
- Planned amounts you entered are saved for the current budget period

**Start from scratch:**
- No categories are created automatically
- Language, currency, and onboarding-completed flag are still saved

### After onboarding

You land on the **Budget** screen with the period and settings you chose. Use the Budget menu to add sections/categories, or **More** for backup, recurring templates, and other features.

### Tips

1. **Suggested categories** are faster if you want a ready-made structure; **scratch** suits users who already know their category list
2. You can change language, currency, and all categories after onboarding
3. Planned amounts from onboarding are starting points—you can tap planned values on the Budget screen anytime to adjust

---

---

# Budget screen

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/budget

The Budget Screen is the main screen of Budgetum where you can view and manage your budget for either a calendar month or a custom budget period. It shows how much you planned to spend or earn, how much you’ve actually spent or received so far, and how you’re tracking toward your goals.

## Accessing the Budget Screen

The Budget Screen is the app’s home screen. You can access it by:
- Opening the app (it opens by default)
- Tapping the **Budget** tab in the bottom navigation

---

## Screen Structure

### Rating invitation

After either 7 elapsed days since the recorded first-open date or at least 10 saved transactions across the app, an **Enjoying Budgetum?** card can appear below the summary and before the remaining budget content. If the summary is hidden, the card is at the top of the scrollable content. It is available to free and Pro users; previous rating-invitation dismissals or rating actions can prevent it from appearing.

- **× / Close**, at the top right of the card, permanently hides it on Budget and clears the rating-related dot on **More**. The More rating card remains available without a close button. Restarting the app or changing periods does not bring the Budget card back.
- **Rate App** opens the App Store review form on iOS or the Google Play listing on Android, where you select the stars under **Rate this app**. Successfully opening the store hides both invitation cards, even if you return without submitting a rating. If the store cannot open, an error appears and the cards remain available.
- The regular **Rate App** row in More remains available afterward. A separate feedback invitation may still cause a More dot.

See [More — Rate App](https://budgetum.app/help/settings#rate-app) for eligibility details and the separate feedback invitation.

### Add Transaction and favourite shortcut

Long-press the **+** button at the bottom center to open **Favourites**. This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on [Recurring Transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring); those controls are not shown in this shortcut.

### Period selector (top bar)

At the top of the screen you’ll see the currently selected budget period.

This can be:
- A calendar month: **Current month** for the actual current month; otherwise, just the month name if it is in the current year (for example, `September` when the current year is 2026), or the month and year for another year (for example, `September 2025`)
- A custom budget period with its own name
- A custom budget period shown by date range when no name was given

**Actions:**
- **Tap the period name** to open the full period picker
- In the picker, switch between **Month** and **Other Periods**
- The Month tab shows available months with income and expense totals
- The Other Periods tab shows your saved custom budget periods grouped into Future, Active, and Previous
- In the **Other Periods** tab, tap **Add** in the header to create a new custom budget period
- An **Edit** button with a calendar icon (tooltip **Edit**) always appears next to the period name. It opens the editor for whatever is currently selected: the calendar month, or the custom period.

When a past or future calendar month is selected, a **Back to current month** button with a curved back arrow appears without a filled background above the Summary Card and stays visible while the budget content scrolls. Tap it to select the current calendar month and show its budget immediately, without opening the period picker or a confirmation. The button then disappears. If the Summary Card is hidden in Display Settings, the button still appears at the top of the budget content. It is not shown for the current month or for any custom budget period. Returning does not change existing transactions or plans.

### Editing the selected month

When a calendar month is selected, tap **Edit** next to the period name. The screen title is that month (for example, `September 2026`).

**Budget amount (optional)**
- Tap the field to open the Number Picker (titled **Budget amount**)
- Helper text: **Leave empty to use planned income.**
- Clear a saved amount with the **×** on the field
- Entering 0 is treated as empty
- If you set an amount greater than 0, the Summary Card’s first column is labeled **Budget** instead of **Income**, and that amount is used as the period’s main income/budget total instead of planned income from income categories

**Income section**
- Switch labeled **Income section**
- Helper: **Show or hide the income section on the budget screen.**
- On (the default): income categories and income totals appear as usual
- Off: the income section is hidden on Budget for that month

Tap the checkmark in the top bar to save. Leaving without saving (Back or close) discards the changes. These month settings apply only to that calendar month and are separate from a custom period’s settings.

When a custom period is selected:
- The same **Edit** button opens the custom period editor (see [Custom Budget Periods](https://budgetum.app/help/custom-budget-periods))
- A small history icon appears in the title if the period is already in the past
- The Budget screen uses that period's exact date range instead of a calendar month

### Top-right actions

The Budget screen has three main actions in the top-right corner:
- **Analytics** (pie chart) — opens **Analytics & Reports** for the currently selected budget period
- **Settings** — opens **Display Settings** directly so you can quickly change how the Budget screen looks and what totals mean
- **Menu** (☰) — opens additional actions

The menu icon (☰) opens:
- **New Expense Section** — create a new budget section to group categories
- **Add Category** — add a new income or expense category
- **Change Order** — rearrange sections and categories
- **Display Settings** — another way to open the same display/settings screen
- **Copy Plan** — import selected category plans from another month or custom period into the current one
- **Export PDF** — configure export settings, create a PDF snapshot, or generate a link to a web copy of the current budget plan
- **Collapse Sections** — collapse all sections at once for a more compact view

---

## Summary Card

At the top of the budget screen there’s a Summary Card showing your overall financial picture for the currently selected period.

### Three-column view
When you have both income and expenses:
- **Income** — planned income (gray) and actual income received (income color). If the selected month or custom period has a **Budget amount** set, this column is labeled **Budget** instead of **Income**
- **Expenses** — planned expenses (gray) and actual spending (primary color)
- **Remaining** — the difference between income and expenses

### Visual indicators
- **Progress bars** between columns fill from bottom to top against the summary’s planned amounts. Above the expense plan, the full bar represents total spending: the primary-colored lower portion is covered by the plan and the red upper portion is the excess, separated by a thin divider. A plan of 500 with 1,000 spent produces equal portions. Small excesses keep their exact proportions, without a minimum red size or extra text.
- The same expense split appears in the horizontal bar when only expenses are shown and in the expanded **Needs** and **Wants** bars. **Income** and **Savings** progress use the income color for the planned share and a lighter green for amounts above a positive plan, with a thin divider between them.
- Progress requires planned values to be enabled and a positive actual amount. A zero or missing plan does not hide progress: expenses show fully red, while income and Savings show fully in the income color, without a divider. This applies to vertical summary bars, single-line bars, and the expanded type bars. Zero or negative actual amounts have no progress fill.
- These indicators use the summary’s planned totals, including adjustments from **Include category overspending in summary totals**, so they can differ from individual section or category indicators.
- **Colored amounts** indicate status:
  - Income color — income or a positive balance
  - Primary color — expenses within budget
  - Red — overspending or a negative balance
- **Difference** shows how much you’re over or under your plan

### Expense breakdown (tap to expand)
If your expenses are grouped by type (Needs, Wants, Savings), tap the Summary Card to expand and see:
- **Needs** (🔒) — essential expenses like rent, utilities, groceries
- **Wants** (❤️) — non-essential spending like entertainment, dining out, fun purchases
- **Savings** (🐷) — money set aside for savings and investments

Each type shows:
- Percentage of total expenses
- Planned vs actual amounts
- Progress bar toward the plan

**Filter by type:** Tap **Needs**, **Wants**, or **Savings** to filter the entire budget view and show only categories of that type.

---

## Visual circles mode (optional)

If **Circle Shortcuts** is enabled under **Display Settings → Circles**, a grid of circular progress indicators appears near the top of the Budget screen (up to five section circles per row). You can tap anywhere in a circle's surrounding tile to open it:
- The Income circle appears only when the section has at least one category available in the selected budget. It remains visible even when the selected month or budget period has no income plans or transactions, unless income is hidden in that budget’s settings. **Show all sections** overrides that hiding for circle shortcuts. Selecting a Needs / Wants / Savings filter hides income circles.
- Each circle shows the section icon and fills based on spending progress
- A fully filled circle means you’ve reached the budget limit
- A red segment in an expense circle indicates the portion of spending above its plan
- With progress shown, section and category circles use the same proportional split as the section and category bars described below, without reducing border opacity for missing plans. Expense activity above a zero or missing plan displays a full red ring.
- With progress hidden for sections or categories, circles with a non-zero actual amount show a complete, solid border in their section color, regardless of the plan or overspending. Circles with a zero actual amount use the same muted neutral border as the unfilled track when progress is shown. Icons and category names keep their usual appearance.

To show unused sections too, open the Budget screen’s top-right **Settings** (gear) → **Circles** and turn on **Show all sections**. This is off by default and is disabled while **Circle Shortcuts** is off. Your choice is saved, including when you switch circles off and back on. Return to Budget to see the change.

- With **Show all sections** off, expense shortcuts require at least one category with a plan or transactions in the selected period. The Income exception above still applies.
- With it on, all sections with categories are available, including sections outside the selected custom budget and income sections hidden from the budget list. Sections without selectable categories are omitted. This affects circle shortcuts; it does not add plans or change the section list or budget totals.
- Circle amounts and progress use the selected month or custom date range. With **Show all sections** on, they include activity in categories excluded from a restricted custom budget. The main budget totals and section list still follow that budget’s restrictions, so circle amounts can differ from the budget list. Adding a transaction through an excluded category’s circle does not link that category to the custom budget; it can remain excluded from its totals.
- Needs / Wants / Savings still filters the shortcuts. With **Show all sections** on, matching categories without plans or transactions remain available.
- When **Show all sections** is on and a section has no categories with plans or transactions matching the active filter, tapping it shows its available categories immediately. Otherwise, unused categories remain behind the reveal control described below.

**Tapping a section circle** opens a bottom sheet for that section. The sheet shows:
- A short **section summary** (name, icon, and the same kinds of spent / planned / remaining / progress details controlled by your section display settings)
- A **grid of category circles** for that section (filtered by Needs / Wants / Savings when that filter is active on the Budget screen). Category names use up to three lines; longer names end with an ellipsis. Long-press a category circle and choose **Edit** to read its full name.
- Optional **actual amount** text under a category circle when your display settings show transaction amounts and the category has a non-zero actual
- If the section has hidden categories, a **Show more (+N)** control reveals them in the same grid

**Tapping a category circle** or its surrounding tile closes the sheet and opens the Add Transaction screen for that category (single-entry / save-and-close mode).

**Long-press a section circle** to open the same options as the section header's long-press or ⋮ menu (see [Section actions](https://budgetum.app/help/budget#section-actions-long-press-or-menu)). **Long-press a category circle**, including its surrounding tile, to close the category picker and open the same options as the category row. The same action availability rules apply as in the list. These shortcuts also work when **Options Button** is off.

To plan an existing unused category, tap its section circle, then **Show more (+N)** if the category is hidden. Long-press the category circle → **Edit** → **Planned Amount**, enter a non-negative amount, then tap the top-right checkmark to save. Saving creates a plan for the selected month or custom budget if the category did not have one. The active Needs / Wants / Savings filter still limits which categories appear; clear or change it on the Budget screen if needed. After editing or dismissing the category options, you return to Budget; tap the section again to reopen its category picker. The unused-category reveal is reset when the picker reopens, unless **Show all sections** automatically reveals those categories because the section has no visible planned or active categories.

There is no longer an Add (plus) circle in circles mode. To add a category, use the section menu in the list below, or **More → Advanced Features → Categories**.

---

## Sets on Budget (Pro)

Turn on **Display Settings → Sets → Show Sets** to show a collapsible Sets block below the Summary Card and circle shortcuts, above the budget sections. **Show Sets** is off by default. Sets has its own switches for actual amounts, planned amounts, remaining amounts, percentages, and progress, independent of the category settings. Only actual amounts are on by default; the other set-item switches are off. Hiding the block or an amount preserves watched sets and saved plans. Sets requires Pro; the switches are disabled without Pro, and the block is hidden. The item switches are disabled while Show Sets is off.

### Add and arrange watched sets

1. Expand the Sets block and tap **Add Set**. If **Action Buttons** is off, long-press the block title or use its **⋮ → Add Set** instead.
2. Tap the **Set** field to open **Select Set**, or tap a quick-select chip below the field. Chips scroll horizontally and select a set without saving the form. The selection page lists sets not already on Budget. Its **search** icon shows a search field; searching matches set names, and hiding search clears it. Its **+** icon opens Create Set; after saving, the new set is selected automatically and you return to the plan form, like other selection pages. The list uses a bordered card with initial-letter circles, like the tag picker. Condition icons beneath each name match the Sets index, including red outlines for excluded conditions. A checkmark identifies the selected set. Back without selecting preserves the form’s selection. If no sets are available, use + to create one.
3. The next row contains **Planned amount**, initially empty. **Plan type** always appears after the amount, including for sets based on tags or other conditions. It defaults to **Expense**; choose **Income** for a positive net target. Editing an existing plan preserves its saved plan type. Fields stack on narrow screens or with larger text. Enter the magnitude as a non-negative number. The plan applies to the budget period from which you opened the form. The amount helper says: “Leave empty to track without a plan.”
4. Tap the top-right checkmark to save. Back without saving discards changes to this form; a set already created from the selection page remains saved.

Watched sets are global: once added, a set appears in all calendar months and custom periods. You do not add it again each period. On the Sets screen, a link icon beside the set name means it is included here. That set’s menu offers **Add to Budget** or **Unlink from Budget**, which adds or removes it immediately without opening this plan form. **Add to Budget** requires Pro. See [Watching sets on Budget](https://budgetum.app/help/saved-sets#watching-sets-on-budget). **Change Order** in the block's menu opens the existing Sets ordering screen; that order applies both here and on Sets. When opened from Budget, it shows all saved sets, with sets not watched on Budget dimmed to indicate that they are not visible in the block. Dimmed sets remain reorderable; dragging them does not add them to Budget. From the main Sets screen, all entries have normal opacity. Tap the block header to collapse or expand it. The eye icon on the right side of the header shows or hides sets without transactions for this period. A count just after that icon, on the right side of the header, shows how many sets are currently displayed. The same action is in the block menu. Long-press menus remain available when **Options Button** hides ⋮ controls. An empty block explains how to add sets. Loading shows a progress indicator; a load failure offers a retry instead of showing zero totals.

### Amounts and matching transactions

With the default set-item switches, each row shows the set’s name and actual net amount. Income minus expenses determines the net, with refunds included in that calculation. Like category spending amounts, net spending is displayed without a minus sign; net income has a **+** prefix and uses the income section color, whether the plan is empty, zero, or positive. A set with no matching transactions remains visible with 0 unless you hide empty sets. The eye icon on the Sets header and **Hide sets without transactions** in the block menu hide watched sets with no matching transactions in the selected period, including recurring previews when future transactions are included. Hiding empty sets does not unlink them. If every watched set is hidden, the block explains that none have transactions in this period. Change Order still lists all saved sets. Currency formatting and Hide numbers apply as elsewhere in Budget.

The block uses the **selected budget period's dates**, replacing each set's saved dates for this view without editing the set. All other set conditions still apply. The block does not restrict sets to a custom budget's selected categories and does not apply the Needs / Wants / Savings filter. Its amounts can therefore cover transactions outside the main budget sections. Set amounts and plans never add to Budget's main summary totals.

**Include future transactions in budget** controls saved future/planned transactions and matching recurring previews in the Budget block's amounts. When off, both are excluded from those amounts. Tap a set row, or choose **Transactions** in its menu, to open the set's transactions for the same period. The transaction screen uses its usual History and Upcoming views, including matching future transactions and recurring previews regardless of this Budget setting. Returning keeps the Budget period and watched sets. **Analytics** opens the set's analytics for the selected dates, using that screen's usual controls.

The Sets block has no combined total. Its rows are independent views of their matching transactions. The Sets block is not included in budget PDF exports or web-share snapshots.

### Set plans

Plan amounts are separate for every month or custom period, with no automatic carryover. An empty Planned amount means there is no plan for that period. Remaining, percentage, progress, and the planned value are hidden; the actual net appears beside the name when any amount or progress switch is enabled. New plans start empty. Entering **0** saves a real zero plan and enables plan comparisons according to the display switches. **× / Clear plan** empties the field, including when it contains 0; save to remove the plan for this period without unlinking the set.

- **Edit Set Plan** in a row's ⋮ or long-press menu opens the same Planned amount / Plan type form with the set fixed. The amount changes only the displayed period. The plan type is global for that watched set and controls plan comparisons across periods; it does not change the set's conditions or displayed net.
- **Expense** compares the plan against expenses minus income and refunds. A plan of 500, expenses of 400, and income of 100 means 300 net spending and 200 left.
- **Income** compares the plan against income minus expenses. A plan of 500, income of 700, and expenses of 300 means 400 net income and 100 left to reach the target.
- Tap **Planned amount** to open the Number Picker. Negative amounts are not allowed. Clear the field with × to remove the plan, or confirm 0 in the picker to save a zero plan. Save with the top-right checkmark; Back discards unsaved changes.
- **Display Settings → Sets** has the same item controls as categories, but changing them affects only set rows: **Total Transaction Amount**, **Planned Amount**, **Remaining/Overspent**, **Percentage of Remaining/Overspent**, and **Progress Indicator**. Rows use the category layout: remaining or over-plan amounts beside the name, actual / planned amounts below, the remaining percentage on the right, and a progress bar underneath when enabled. Percentage is remaining divided by plan (for example, 50 spent against 100 planned leaves 50%). Above a positive plan it shows the excess percentage in the same color as category over-plan values. At exactly the plan, the remaining amount and percentage are hidden. With a saved 0 plan, the planned amount shows 0 when enabled. Positive activity in the plan’s direction is entirely over plan: the percentage shows 100%, and progress is fully filled (red for Expense plans, income color for Income plans). With no activity, remaining and percentage are hidden and progress has no fill. Activity opposite to the plan’s direction shows 0% and no progress fill. Only an empty plan hides all plan comparisons and disables over-plan coloring. These switches work independently, so **Percentage of Remaining/Overspent** can be shown while **Planned Amount** is hidden.
- When the planned value is visible and **Quick plan update** is on, tap its dotted underline in the Budget row to update this period's amount directly. With Quick plan update off, use **Edit Set Plan**. The quick picker may offer the current positive net amount in the plan's direction as a shortcut.
- **Copy Plan** includes eligible watched sets alongside categories. Choose the source period, select the sets to copy, and save. Only sets with a saved source plan and an empty destination plan appear. A saved 0 plan can be copied and prevents an existing destination plan from being overwritten. Clear the destination plan first if you want to copy another plan into that period. Copying changes neither the global watched list nor plan types. Set plans can be copied even while their Budget display is hidden. Deleted custom periods are not available as Copy Plan sources.

**Edit Set** opens the full filter editor and preserves the Budget selection and plans. **Unlink from Budget** uses a broken-link icon and immediately removes the set from this block in every period, without deleting the saved set or its period plans. Adding it again restores any plan saved for the selected period. Deleting the saved set itself on Sets removes it and its plans.

---

## Budget sections

Your budget is organized into sections (for example, “Housing”, “Transportation”, “Income”, etc.). Each section contains related categories.

### Section header
Each section shows:
- **Section icon and name** — its identity with a custom color
- **Arrow indicator** — whether the section is expanded (↑) or collapsed (↓)
- **Amount left** or **Amount spent** — depending on your display settings
- **Progress bar** (optional) — visual indicator of spending vs plan
- **Percentage** (optional) — how much of the budget is used or remaining

### Expand/collapse sections
- **Tap anywhere on the section header** to expand or collapse it
- Expanded sections show all categories inside
- The app remembers which sections you expanded

### Section actions (long press or menu)
Long-press a section header (or tap the ⋮ menu if it’s shown) to access:
- **New Income Source** or **New Expense Category** — add a new category to this section (label depends on section type)
- **Transactions** — view all transactions in this section
- **Trends** — view a plan vs actual chart by month
- **Analytics** — open charts and reports for this section
- **Edit** — change the section name, icon, or color
- **Delete Plan** — remove the budget plan (only if there are no transactions)
- **Delete** — permanently remove the section (only if it has no categories)

---

## Budget categories

Inside each section you’ll see categories (for example, “Groceries”, “Electricity”, “Salary”, etc.).

### Category display
Each category shows:
- **Category name** — with a recurring icon (↻) if it’s linked to recurring transactions
- **Amount left** or **Amount spent** — depending on your display settings
- **Spent / Planned** — actual spending versus the budgeted amount
- **Tappable planned amount** — when planned amounts are visible and **Quick plan update** is on, the planned value is shown with a subtle dotted underline to indicate that you can tap it. When **Quick plan update** is off, the amount is not underlined and is not tappable
- **Percentage** — how much of the category budget is used or remaining
- **Progress bar** (optional) — visual indicator of spending progress

### Color coding
- **Section color** — normal spending within budget
- **Red** — overspending (exceeded the planned amount)
- **Gray** — remaining amount to spend

Section and category progress bars, circle rings, and the section summary bar inside the circle category picker show exact proportions:
- Up to the plan, the section-colored fill shows actual spending relative to the plan; the rest is an empty gray track. A plan of 500 with 250 spent fills half the indicator.
- Above an expense plan, the full indicator represents total spending. The section-colored portion is the amount covered by the plan; the red portion is the excess. A plan of 500 with 1,000 spent is half section color and half red; with 600 spent, one-sixth is red.
- A thin divider marks where the section-colored portion meets the red excess in bars and rings. It appears only when both portions are present; it does not enlarge the red portion.
- Red segments have no minimum size. Spending 501 against a 500 plan produces a very small red segment that may be hard to see. Existing amount colors still apply; no additional overspending label is added.
- Positive expense spending with a zero or missing plan is fully red. Zero or negative net spending (for example, after refunds) leaves the indicator empty.
- Income uses its section color up to the plan. Above a positive income plan, bars and rings show the planned share in the section color and the surplus in a lighter green, separated by a thin divider. With 500 planned and 1,000 received, each portion occupies half the indicator. Positive income with a zero or missing plan keeps a full section-colored indicator. No divider appears at or below the plan, or with a zero or missing plan.

These rules apply when the corresponding section or category progress display is enabled. The summary card’s indicators and their display conditions are described under **Summary Card** above.

### Category actions
**Tap a category** to view all transactions for that category.

**Tap the planned amount** in the category row to quickly change that category’s planned value without opening the full edit screen. This is available only when **Quick plan update** is on in Display Settings (it is on by default). It opens the Number Picker with the current planned amount prefilled. If the category has actual spending, the picker can also offer that spent amount as a one-tap quick-select value. When **Quick plan update** is off, use **Edit** on the category instead.

**Long-press a category** (or tap the ⋮ menu if shown) to access:
- **Add Transaction** — quickly add a new transaction to this category
- **Transactions** — view all transactions for this category
- **Trends** — view a plan vs actual chart by month
- **Analytics** — open charts and detailed reports
- **Edit** — change the category name, planned amount, or settings
- **Delete Plan** — remove the budget plan for this month (only if there are no transactions)
- **Delete** — permanently remove the category (only if there are no transactions and no recurring templates)

### Adding categories to a section
At the bottom of each expanded section there’s a **New Income Source** or **New Expense Category** button to quickly create a new category within that section. These in-list buttons appear only when **Action Buttons** is on in Display Settings (it is on by default). The ☰ menu still offers **Add Category** when the buttons are hidden.

---

## Edit Section screen

Opened when you choose **Edit** from a section’s long-press or ⋮ menu. Use it to change the section’s identity and appearance.

**Fields and actions:**
- **Section name** — text field; required. Duplicate names (compared to other sections) are not allowed.
- **Icon** — tap to open an icon picker (bottom sheet). Different icon sets for income vs expense sections.
- **Color** — tap to open a color picker: “Default” (app primary) or a grid of preset colors.

**Saving:** Tap the ✓ (check) button in the app bar. Validation runs before save (non-empty name, no duplicate).

---

## Edit Category screen

Opened when you choose **Edit** from a category’s long-press or ⋮ menu. Use it to change the category’s name, section, type, and (when editing from the budget) its planned amount.

**Fields and actions:**
- **Section** — read-only for income categories; for expense categories, tap to open a section picker and move the category to another expense section.
- **Category name** — text field; required. Duplicate names (compared to other categories) are not allowed.
- **Category type** (expense categories only) — **Needs**, **Wants**, or **Savings** with short descriptions. Used for the Summary Card breakdown and filtering.
- **Planned amount** (when not hidden) — tap to open a number picker. Required and must be ≥ 0. An icon opens **History** for this category (spending history screen).
- **Last months’ history** — when the category has plan/actual data, a block shows the last several months with planned vs actual amounts and a progress bar. Tap an **actual** or **planned** amount to copy it into the planned amount field for the current month.

**Saving:** Tap the ✓ (check) button in the app bar. Validation: non-empty name, no duplicate name, valid amount (when amount is shown). When opened from the budget screen, both the category and its plan are updated; when opened from elsewhere (e.g. categories screen) with plan hidden, only the category (name, section, type) is updated.

---

## Quick actions

### Copy a budget plan from another period
If you’re starting a new month or custom period and want to use an existing plan as a template:
1. Tap the menu button (☰) in the top right
2. Select **Copy Plan**
3. Choose the month or custom period you want to copy from
4. Review the list of category plans from that source period
5. Select the categories you want to import, then tap the check button to apply them

Important details:
- Budgetum imports only the **selected category plans**, not a forced full clone of the entire source budget
- Categories that already exist in the current target period are skipped and do not appear in the import list
- When a previous plan source is found automatically, Budgetum preselects all eligible categories so you can import them faster

A **Copy Plan** button also appears below the sections when **Action Buttons** is on, the current selection has at most one category with a plan, and other plan sources are available. The ☰ menu still offers **Copy Plan** when the in-list button is hidden.

#### New month reminder
When a new calendar month starts, the Budget screen can ask **A new month has started**. The dialog shows last month (for example, **From last month: November 2026**) and offers **Copy Plan** and **Not now**. **Copy Plan** switches Budget to the current month if last month was still selected, then opens the same Copy Plan screen with last month already chosen as the source and all its categories preselected; review them, untick any you don't need, and tap the check button to copy. **Not now** (or tapping outside) closes the dialog; you can still use **Copy Plan** from the ☰ menu at any time.

The reminder appears at most once per month, when you open the app or return to it from the background while the Budget tab is shown and no other screen is open. If you are on another tab at that moment, it waits until the next time. It appears only if:
- the current month or last month is selected (not an older or later month, and not a custom period). Budget reopens on the month you viewed last, so on the first open of a new month it usually still shows last month
- last month has plans (category plans, or set plans with Pro)
- this month has no plans yet (no category plans, and no set plans with Pro); once you plan anything in the new month, the reminder is not shown

If last month had no plans, Budgetum does not ask, even when an older month or a custom period has plans. Ended custom periods have their own dialog; see [Custom Budget Periods](https://budgetum.app/help/custom-budget-periods#when-a-period-ends).

### Export budget as PDF or web link
Use **Export PDF** from the Budget screen menu to open the budget export flow for the period you are currently viewing.

**Export settings** (gear icon on the export screen):
- **Group by expense type** — group expense categories under Needs, Wants, and Savings when applicable
- **Show section titles** — include section headings in the output
- **Show planned values** / **Show actual values** — at least one must stay on; both can be included in PDF and web share

**PDF preview:**
- Live preview of the report; use the system share/print actions from the preview bar to save or send the PDF

**Web share link** (link icon on the preview bar):
- Generates a read-only web view of the budget plan for the selected period
- Choose whether the shared view includes planned and/or actual amounts (at least one required)
- Copy the URL to share; links expire after a limited number of days (shown when the link is ready)

Other details:
- The export follows the active period selector (month or custom budget period)
- Change the selected period on the Budget screen before exporting if you need a different range
- Shared links expose budget structure and amounts you include—share only with people you trust

### “New Expense Section” button
Below your existing sections (and the Copy Plan button when it’s shown) there’s a **New Expense Section** button to create a new budget grouping. It appears only when **Action Buttons** is on. The ☰ menu still offers **New Expense Section** when the button is hidden.

---

## Getting started help

When you first start using the app, a helpful guide appears at the bottom of the Budget Screen with tips on:
- Making a list of expected expenses for the month
- Grouping them into sections
- Adding transactions to track actual expenses

It also shows section examples (e.g. Housing, Travel, Car). You can dismiss this guide once you’re comfortable.

---

## Display customization

You can customize the Budget Screen to show exactly what you need. Open **Display Settings** from the top-right **Settings** button or from the menu.

### General options
- **Quick plan update** — tap a category’s planned amount to update it directly. On by default. When off, the planned amount is not tappable or underlined.
- **Options Button** — show or hide the ⋮ menu buttons on sections and categories. When off, options appear on long press instead of a button.
- **Action Buttons** — show buttons for adding sections and categories or copying a plan. On by default. When off, the in-list **Copy Plan**, **New Expense Section**, and **New Income Source** / **New Expense Category** buttons are hidden; the ☰ menu still has those actions.
- **Include Upcoming Transactions in Budget** — include or exclude future-dated transactions from the current budget totals. When this is on, upcoming transactions already affect the Budget screen's actual totals and progress bars. When it is off, the Budget screen only counts transactions that are not in the future.

### Circles options
- **Circle Shortcuts** — show or hide the section circle grid; on by default.
- **Show all sections** — include all sections with categories, regardless of the selected budget; off by default. Available only while **Circle Shortcuts** is on. See [Visual circles mode](https://budgetum.app/help/budget#visual-circles-mode-optional) for display rules and tapping behavior.

### Summary card options
- **Hide summary card** — hide the Summary Card on the Budget screen. Off by default. When it is on, the card is gone; the **Back to current month** button still appears when a past or future calendar month is selected.
- Show/hide planned values
- Show/hide actual values
- Show/hide the difference column/value
- **Hide Decimals** — show Summary Card amounts rounded to whole numbers (for example `1,235` instead of `1,234.56`). On by default. Turn it off to see exact amounts with cents in the Income, Expenses, and remaining values. The Needs / Wants / Savings amounts on the card follow the same setting. Applies to the Budget screen only. Only display changes; totals are calculated from the exact amounts either way.
- Include category overspending in summary totals. When this is on, any amount spent above a category's plan is added to the summary card's planned totals, so the overall remaining amount reflects that overspending more realistically.

If either planned values or actual values are hidden, the **Difference** setting becomes unavailable because the comparison needs both values.

### Section display options
- Show/hide planned amounts
- Show/hide spent amounts
- Show/hide remaining amounts
- Show/hide remaining percentage
- Show/hide progress bars

### Category display options
- Show/hide planned amounts
- Show/hide spent amounts
- Show/hide remaining amounts
- Show/hide remaining percentage
- Show/hide progress bars

---

## Tips for using the Budget Screen

1. **Check it regularly** — open the Budget Screen daily or weekly
2. **Use sections wisely** — group related expenses for easier management
3. **Watch the colors** — red means overspending
4. **Tap for details** — tap any category to see exactly where your money went
5. **Filter by type** — focus on Needs, Wants, or Savings
6. **Copy previous budgets** — use **Copy Plan** to save time

---

# Custom budget periods

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/custom-budget-periods

Custom Budget Periods let you budget across any date range instead of being limited to a calendar month. You can create named or unnamed periods, switch the Budget screen into that period, and keep separate plans for those custom ranges.

This feature is managed from the Budget screen's period picker.

---

## Accessing Custom Budget Periods

You can access custom budget periods by:
- Opening the **Budget** screen
- Tapping the current period in the top bar
- Switching from **Month** to **Other Periods**

An **Edit** button with a calendar icon (tooltip **Edit**) always appears next to the period name in the Budget screen header. When a custom period is selected, it opens that period’s editor. When a calendar month is selected, it opens the month editor instead (see [Budget Screen](https://budgetum.app/help/budget#editing-the-selected-month)).

---

## What a Custom Budget Period Changes

When you select a custom period:
- The Budget screen uses that period's **start** and **end** dates instead of a calendar month
- Budget plans are loaded from that custom period instead of monthly plans
- Transactions and recurring previews are limited to that selected date range
- The top bar shows the custom period name, or its date range if it has no name

If the selected period ends before today, the Budget screen header also shows a small history icon to make it clear that you are viewing a past period.

---

## Period Picker Layout

The Budget period picker opens as a full-screen selector with two tabs in the title area:
- **Month** - Standard month-based budgeting
- **Other Periods** - Your custom budget periods

### Month Tab

The Month tab works like the normal month selector:
- Choose any month
- See income and expense totals on the tiles
- Switch the global budget view back to monthly mode

Selecting a month automatically clears the active custom budget period and returns the app to month-based budgeting.

### Other Periods Tab

The Other Periods tab shows your saved custom periods grouped by timing:
- **Future** - Periods that have not started yet
- **Active** - Periods that include today
- **Previous** - Periods that already ended

Future and Previous groups can be collapsed or expanded. The Active group stays open. Previous periods load their totals when the group is expanded.

If there are no saved custom periods yet, the screen shows an empty state with a button to create one.

### Period Card Information

Each custom period card can show:
- **Name** - Optional custom title
- **Date range** - The start and end dates
- **Planned badges** - Planned income and planned expenses
- **Actual badges** - Actual income and actual expenses in the period
- **Trailing total** - The current remainder/balance for the period
- **Selection highlight** - Indicates the active budget period
- **More button** - Opens actions for that period

If a period has a custom name, the picker shows that name with the date range underneath. If there is no custom name, the date range is used as the main title.

---

## Selecting a Custom Period

Tap a period card to switch the Budget screen to that period.

When the picker is being used for full budget switching:
- The selected custom period becomes the active budget scope
- The Budget screen reloads immediately
- The picker closes after the new period is applied

The **Use this period** action in the more menu does the same thing.

---

## Creating or Editing a Custom Period

Use the **Add** button in the picker header, or open an existing period and choose **Edit**.

The editor contains these fields:

### Name

- **Optional**
- Lets you give the period a short label like `Paycheck Cycle`, `Vacation`, or `School Term`
- If left empty, Budgetum displays the date range instead

### Start Date and End Date

- Define the exact inclusive range of the period
- If you move one boundary past the other, the editor automatically keeps the dates in a valid order

### Budget Amount

- **Optional**
- If left empty, planned income is based on the period's income-category plans
- If set, the custom amount becomes the period's main income/budget total on the Budget screen

### All Transactions

This switch controls whether the Budget screen includes only planned categories or the full category set inside the date range.

- **On** - Show all transactions in the selected date range, including categories that do not have a plan in this custom period
- **Off** - Limit the budget view to categories linked to this custom period's plans (while still allowing related planned sections to appear)

### Income Section

This switch controls whether the income section is visible while that custom period is active.

- **On** - Show income categories and income totals normally
- **Off** - Hide the income section from the Budget screen for this period

### Saving

Tap the **checkmark** in the top bar to save the period.

When you create a new period from the picker, Budgetum saves it, reloads the list, and automatically switches the Budget screen to the newly created period.

---

## Managing Existing Periods

Open the more menu on a period card, or long-press the card, to access:
- **Use this period** - Apply it to the Budget screen
- **Edit** - Change its name, dates, or options
- **Delete** - Remove the custom period after confirmation

Deleting a custom period also deletes the plans stored specifically for that period.

If you delete the period that is currently selected, Budgetum returns the budget view to normal month mode.

---

## When a Period Ends

If the custom period selected on the Budget screen has ended, Budgetum asks once what to do next. The dialog appears the next time you open the app or return to it from the background while the Budget tab is shown and no other screen is open. If you are on another tab at that moment, it waits until the next time. It is titled **"<period> has ended"**, using the period's name or its date range, and shows the next dates.

- **Not now** — closes the dialog. The period stays selected and the dialog does not appear again for it. Tapping outside the dialog does the same.
- **Move dates** — keeps the same period and changes its dates to the next ones. Its plans and settings stay as they are. The period's previous results are no longer shown as a separate period; your transactions are not changed. When the new dates end, Budgetum asks again.
- **Create next period** — creates a new period with the next dates and selects it. The new period gets the same Budget amount, **All Transactions** and **Income Section** settings, and a copy of all category plans and set plans. The ended period stays unchanged in the **Previous** group.

**Next dates:**
- A period covering whole months continues by the same number of months, following the calendar. For example, Sep 1 – Sep 30 continues as Oct 1 – Oct 31, Sep 15 – Oct 14 as Oct 15 – Nov 14, and Jan 1 – Dec 31 as the next full year.
- Any other period continues with the same number of days. For example, a 14-day period Sep 6 – Sep 19 continues as Sep 20 – Oct 3.
- If several cycles were missed while the app was not opened, Budgetum goes straight to the cycle that includes today. It does not create the periods in between.

**Name:** if the name ends with its only number, the number goes up by one per cycle: `Paycheck 3` becomes `Paycheck 4`, and `Budget 2026` becomes `Budget 2027`. Other names are kept as they are, including names with a date range or more than one number. Two periods can have the same name; the picker shows each one's dates.

**When the dialog does not appear:**
- The period has no plans: no category or section plans, no set plans, and no Budget amount.
- A period with exactly the next dates already exists.
- You chose an already-ended period in the picker, for example to review past spending from **Previous**.
- You saved the period in the editor with an end date in the past.
- The dialog was already shown for this period, even if the app was closed without answering it.
- The selected period has not ended yet, or a calendar month is selected.

---

## Using Plans with Custom Periods

Custom periods keep their own budget plans, separate from monthly plans.

This means:
- A category can have one plan for `March 2026` and a different plan for a custom period that overlaps March
- Copy/import plan actions can use monthly plans or another custom period as the source
- Reopening the same custom period restores its saved plan values

This also makes custom periods useful as **plan templates**. For example, you can keep reusable periods for things like pay cycles, travel budgets, seasonal spending, or event planning, then copy those plans into a new month or another custom period when needed.

---

## Tips for Using Custom Budget Periods

1. **Name repeated periods clearly** - Labels like `Paycheck 1`, `Paycheck 2`, or `Summer Trip` make them easier to recognize in the picker.
2. **Use a custom budget amount for fixed-cycle budgeting** - This is helpful when you budget against a paycheck amount rather than planned income categories.
3. **Turn off All Transactions for stricter budgeting** - This keeps the view focused on categories that are actually part of the custom plan.
4. **Hide income when it is not useful** - For spending-only periods, turning off the income section can simplify the screen.
5. **Review past periods from the Previous group** - It is useful for checking completed trips, pay cycles, or short-term plans without changing your monthly history.

---

# Transactions screen

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/transactions

The Transactions Screen shows **budget transactions** for the budget period you select - that is, income and expense transactions that are linked to your budget categories. This includes transactions from all accounts but excludes pure transfers between accounts and balance adjustments (unless they're combined with a categorized transaction). Transactions are organized by date so you can review your financial activity and track spending for the chosen period.

## Accessing the Transactions Screen

You can access the Transactions Screen by:
- Tapping the "Transactions" tab in the bottom navigation

If there are scheduled transactions that still require confirmation, the Transactions tab shows a small question-mark badge as a reminder.

---

## Screen Layout

### Period Selector (Top Bar)

At the top of the screen, the **selected budget period** is displayed.

This can be:
- A calendar month: **Current month** for the actual current month; otherwise, just the month name if it is in the current year (for example, `September` when the current year is 2026), or the month and year for another year (for example, `September 2025`)
- A custom budget period with its own name
- A custom budget period shown by date range when it has no name

All data on the screen - summary and transaction list - follows that selected budget period.

**Actions:**
- **Tap the period name** to open the budget period picker
- Switch between **Month** and **Other Periods**
- Choose another month or a saved custom budget period

When a past or future calendar month is selected, a **Back to current month** button with a curved back arrow appears without a filled background above the Summary Card. It stays visible while the transaction list scrolls. Tap it to return to the current calendar month without opening the period picker or a confirmation; the summary and list update, and the button disappears. The selected History or Upcoming view is preserved. The button is hidden for the current month and for all custom budget periods. Returning does not change existing transactions or plans.

### Top Bar Buttons

The top bar contains several action buttons:

- **Calendar Icon** - Opens the Daily Transactions view where you can browse transactions by specific dates on a calendar
- **Repeat Icon** - Opens the Recurring Transactions screen to manage subscriptions, bills, and regular income
- **Search Icon** - Opens the Transaction Search screen to find specific transactions

For charts and spending insights, use **Analytics** from the Budget screen (pie chart icon in the top bar) or from category/section menus elsewhere in the app.

---

## Summary Card

At the top of the transactions list, a Summary Card shows **income, expenses, and balance for the selected budget period**. The totals include all budget transactions (those linked to budget categories) in that period, including both past and upcoming.

### Three-Column View
When you have both income and expenses:
- **Income** – Total money received (shown in income color)
- **Expenses** – Total money spent (shown in the app's primary color)
- **Balance** – The difference between income and expenses

### Visual Indicators
- **Income color** = Income or positive balance
- **Primary color** = Expenses
- **Red** = Negative balance (expenses exceed income)

### Single-Line View
If you only have income or only have expenses for the selected period, the Summary Card displays a simplified single-line format showing just that information.

---

## History and Upcoming Tabs

When you have both past transactions and future scheduled transactions (and each section has at least some income or expenses), the screen displays two toggle buttons:

### History Tab
Shows all transactions from today and earlier, sorted with the most recent transactions first.

### Upcoming Tab
Shows all future transactions (scheduled, recurring, or planned), sorted with the soonest transactions first.

**Tab Information:**
- Each tab displays the total income and expenses for that section
- Income is shown in income color with a "+" prefix
- Expenses are shown in red with a "-" prefix
- Tap a tab to switch between History and Upcoming views

**Note:** If you only have past transactions or only have future transactions, the tabs won't appear—the screen will automatically show whichever section has data. Tabs also won't appear if one section has only transfers or balance adjustments (no income or expenses).

---

## Confirmation Required Block

If you have recurring transactions that require confirmation before being applied, they appear in a special highlighted section at the top of the transaction list.

**What are confirmation-required transactions?**
These are scheduled transactions that need your approval before they affect your account balances. This is useful for recurring expenses that may vary in amount or that you want to verify before recording.

**Actions:**
- **Tap a confirmation-required transaction** to open options for confirming, skipping, or modifying it

---

## Transaction List

The list shows **budget transactions** for the selected budget period - that is, income and expense transactions linked to budget categories. Transactions are grouped by date with clear date headers. Each date section shows all transactions that occurred on that day. Within a day, transactions from the same receipt or the same contact may appear as a grouped row with a header - tap the group to open the full list for that receipt or contact.

### Transaction Display

Each transaction shows:
- **Category icon** (on the left) - The icon of the budget section this transaction belongs to
- **Category name** - The budget category (e.g., "Groceries", "Salary", "Rent")
- **Amount** (on the right) - The transaction amount with color coding:
  - Income color with "+" prefix = Income
  - Section color = Expenses (matches the category's budget section color)

### Additional Transaction Details

Transactions may also display:
- **Receipt icon** - Shown after the category name when this row belongs to a receipt. Several items from the same receipt on the same day still appear as one group. If every item in that group uses the same category, the group title is that category name with the receipt icon after it. If the items use different categories, the group title is Receipt and the icon on the left is the receipt icon.
- **Recurring icon (↻)** - Indicates this transaction is linked to a recurring template
- **Question mark icon (?)** - Indicates the transaction requires confirmation
- **Swap icon (↔)** - Indicates this is a combined transaction (categorized expense plus transfer between accounts)
- **Contact badge** - Shows which person or business this transaction involves
- **Account badge** - Shows which account was used for this transaction
- **Description** - Any notes you added to the transaction
- **Tags** - Hashtags for additional categorization (shown as #tagname)

### Preview Transactions

Future transactions from recurring templates appear slightly faded to indicate they are previews of upcoming scheduled transactions, not yet confirmed.

---

## Transaction Types

### Regular Transactions (Income/Expenses)
Standard income or expense transactions linked to a budget category. These are the primary transactions shown on this screen.

### Combined Transactions (Expense + Transfer)
Transactions that are both categorized expenses and transfers between accounts. These show:
- A swap icon (↔) indicating a transfer component
- The category name and icon
- The expense amount

**Note:** Pure transfers between accounts, balance adjustments, and initial balances are **not shown** on the Transactions screen since they aren't linked to budget categories. To view those, go to the specific account's transaction history.

---

## Transaction Actions

### Tap a Transaction
**For regular transactions:** Opens the Edit Transaction screen where you can modify all details.

**For preview/recurring transactions:** Opens options to:
- Confirm the transaction
- Skip this occurrence
- Modify the amount or details

**For confirmation-required transactions:** Opens a confirmation dialog with options to confirm, skip, or edit.

### Long-Press a Transaction
Long-pressing a transaction (except preview and confirmation-required ones) opens a quick actions menu with options to:
- Edit the transaction
- Edit receipt, when this transaction belongs to a receipt. Opens that receipt with all of its items, including items outside the current list
- Duplicate the transaction
- Delete the transaction
- Transform to receipt (for eligible expenses that are not already part of a receipt—creates a receipt from the transaction and opens the Add Receipt screen)

---

## Adding New Transactions

At the bottom center of the screen, a single **Add Transaction** floating action button opens the Add Transaction screen where you can record income or expenses.

Long-press the **+** button at the bottom center to open **Favourites**. This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on [Recurring Transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring); those controls are not shown in this shortcut.
