To add a multi-item receipt instead, open **Add Transaction** in expense mode and tap the split icon next to the **Category** field. This opens the Add Receipt screen and carries over the selected account, date, contact, and typed amount when available. A selected category filters the store quick-select chips to contacts recently used with that category.

---

## Loading More Transactions

The screen initially shows a limited number of transactions for faster loading. If you have more transactions:

**"Show More" Button:**
When there are additional transactions to display, a "Show More" button appears at the bottom of the list. Tap it to load more transactions.

The list always shows complete days—if you have many transactions on a single day, all of them will be shown together rather than cutting off mid-day.

---

## Empty State

If there are no transactions for the selected budget period, the screen displays:
- A receipt icon
- A message indicating no transactions exist for that period

This is a good reminder to start recording your income and expenses!

---

## Tips for Using the Transactions Screen

1. **Review regularly** - Check your transactions weekly to catch any errors or forgotten entries
2. **Use the search** - The search function helps you quickly find specific transactions by amount, description, or category
3. **Check upcoming transactions** - Review the Upcoming tab to see what bills and income are coming up
4. **Confirm recurring transactions** - Don't forget to confirm or adjust scheduled transactions that require verification
5. **Use contacts and tags** - Adding contacts and tags to transactions makes it easier to filter and analyze your spending later
6. **Use receipts** - From Add Transaction, use the split icon next to the category field to split one purchase into multiple categorized items
7. **Switch periods easily** - Use the period picker to review past months or saved custom budget periods

---

# Add and edit transactions

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction

The Add Transaction and Edit Transaction screens are where you record and modify your income and expense transactions. These screens provide all the fields you need to accurately track where your money goes and where it comes from.

## Accessing the Add Transaction Screen

You can open the Add Transaction screen by:
- Tapping the "+" button on the main Transactions screen or Budget screen
- Long-pressing that **+** button when favourites exist, then tapping a favourite in the bottom sheet. This opens a prefilled form dated today; if the template amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically. See [Recurring Transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring) for the shortcut and template types.
- Tapping "Add Transaction" from a category's menu on the Budget screen
- Tapping a category circle after opening a section from visual circles mode on the Budget screen (section circle → category bottom sheet → category)
- Using the "+" button when viewing an account's transactions

**Receipt split shortcut (expense mode):** In expense mode, a split icon appears next to the **Category** field. Tap it to open the Add Receipt screen and split one purchase into multiple categorized transactions.

---

## Transaction Types

At the top of the Add Transaction screen, you'll see two toggle options:

### Expense
Records money going out—purchases, bills, payments. This is the default selection.

### Income
Records money coming in—salary, payments received, refunds. Tap "Income" to switch to recording income.

**Note:** When adding transactions from a receipt, only expense mode is available since receipts typically represent purchases.

---

## Transaction Fields

### Amount and Date Row

At the top of the form, you'll see:

**Amount Field:**
- Tap to open the calculator-style number picker
- Enter the transaction amount
- The calculator supports basic math operations (+, −, ×, ÷) for splitting bills or calculating totals
- Your currency symbol appears next to the field
- This top **Amount** field is always the **budget amount** in your app's main currency (the value used by budgets, analytics, and reports)
- When a foreign-currency account is selected, the label can include the main currency code (for example `Amount UAH`) so it stays clear which currency this field uses

**Date Field:**
- Shows the transaction date in a friendly format (e.g., "Today", "Yesterday", "Mon, Jan 20")
- Tap to open the date picker and select a different date
- The date picker shows income and expense totals for each day, helping you navigate your history

### Confirmation Required (Future Dates Only)

When you set a future date, a checkbox appears:

**"Confirmation Required"**
- Enable this if you want to verify the transaction before it affects your budget
- The transaction will appear in the "Confirmation Required" section on the Transactions screen
- Useful for planned expenses that might change in amount

---

### Category

**Category Field:**
- Shows the selected budget category with its section icon and color
- Tap to open the category picker
- Categories are organized into sections (e.g., Food, Transportation, Income)
- For expenses, only expense categories are shown
- For income, income categories are shown; you can also select expense categories for income (e.g. to record refunds or money returned to a spending category)
- Hidden categories within a section can be revealed with **Show more (+N)**; hidden sections (not in the current period) can likewise be revealed with **Show more (+N)** at the bottom of the picker

The category determines:
- Which budget the transaction counts toward
- The color and icon displayed for the transaction
- How the transaction is grouped in reports

For expense transactions, the split icon next to the category field opens **Add Receipt**. Budgetum carries over the selected account, date, contact, and any amount already typed as the receipt total. If a category is selected, store quick-select chips on Add Receipt show contacts recently used with that category. This shortcut is hidden for income, transfers, and transactions that are already part of a receipt.

---

### Account

**From Account / To Account Field:**
- Shows which account this transaction uses
- For expenses: "From Account" (where the money comes from)
- For income: "To Account" (where the money goes)
- Tap to select from your active accounts
- Quick-select chips appear below the field showing your recently used accounts

**Required vs Optional:**
- For regular income/expense transactions, account selection is optional.
- For combined transactions (transfer mode enabled), both account fields become required.
- If you have no active accounts, the account field is hidden and you can still save regular transactions.

**Recently Used Accounts:**
Below the account field, you may see small chips showing accounts you've used recently with this category. Tap a chip to quickly select that account. These suggestions are filtered to accounts that use the app's current main currency, so different-currency accounts are not offered as quick chips.

**Foreign-currency accounts (normal income/expense):**
You can select an account whose currency differs from the app's main currency for a regular expense or income (not only for transfers). When you do:

1. The top **Amount** field remains the **budget amount** in the main currency
2. An extra account amount field appears below the account picker:
   - Expenses: **Debited** (money leaving the account), in the account's currency
   - Income: **Credited** (money entering the account), in the account's currency
3. Both amounts are required when currencies differ. Budgets and reports use the budget amount; the account balance moves by the debited/credited amount
4. Budgetum may offer a **market-rate quick suggestion** in the number picker (based on a live rate lookup). The suggestion is optional—you can accept it or type your own amount. Rates are not saved as a separate exchange-rate history in the app
5. Changing the account to a different currency clears the account-amount field so you can enter the new currency amount

**Receipts stay on the main currency:** When adding or editing a receipt (or a receipt line), account selection is limited to accounts in your current main currency. Foreign-currency accounts are available for normal transactions and for multi-currency transfers, not for receipts.

**Transfer Toggle (↔ button):**
Next to the account field, you'll see a swap icon. Tap it to enable "combined transaction" mode:
- This records both a budget transaction AND an account transfer in one step
- Useful when you pay from one account but want to record money also moving to another account
- When enabled, additional fields appear for the transfer destination and amount
- If either side uses a different currency, you can enter different from/to amounts; a market-rate quick suggestion may appear in the number picker for the other side

---

### Contact

**"Paid to" / "Received from" Field:**
- Track who you paid or who paid you
- For expenses: "Paid to" (store, person, or business)
- For income: "Received from" (employer, client, payer)
- Tap to select an existing contact or create a new one
- Quick-select chips show recently used contacts for this category

**Recently Used Contacts:**
Below the contact field, chips appear showing contacts you've transacted with recently for this category. Tap a chip to quickly select that contact.

**Note:** On the Add Transaction screen, this field only appears if you have the "Show contact on transaction creation" setting enabled. On the Edit Transaction screen, the contact field is always visible so you can view or change it.

---

### Description

**Description Field:**
- Optional. Add extra notes or details about the transaction.
- Examples: "Table 4", "Refund for defective item", "Bonus from Q4 review"
- Tap to type freely
- Supports multiple lines for longer notes

**Recently Used Descriptions:**
Below the description field, chips appear showing descriptions you've used before for this category. Tap anywhere inside a chip, including the space around its text, to quickly fill in that description.

---

### Tags

**Tags Field:**
- Add labels to organize transactions beyond categories
- Multiple tags can be added to a single transaction
- Tags appear as #tagname format
- Tap to open the tag selector where you can:
  - Select existing tags
  - Create new tags
  - Remove selected tags

**Recently Used Tags:**
Below the tags field, chips appear showing tags you've used recently. Tap a chip to quickly add or remove that tag.

**Note:** On the Add Transaction screen, this field only appears if you have the "Show tags on transaction creation" setting enabled. On the Edit Transaction screen, the tags field is always visible so you can view or change tags.

---

### Repeat and Favourites

Tap the **Repeat** row, arrow, or off switch to open repeat options. Turn on **Favourite** at the top to save a reusable template without needing a schedule. When no favourite templates are saved, a small, muted helper beneath the switch explains that favourites let you quickly add transactions without a repeat schedule. It is hidden when you open Repeat with at least one saved favourite. The switch keeps the page open; Back retains the choice in the transaction form. Selecting **Do not repeat** or a repeat preset returns immediately with the favourite choice preserved. Custom opens a separate schedule page; applying it also preserves Favourite.

- **Favourite only:** turn on Favourite, leave Do not repeat selected, return and save the transaction. No automatic transactions are generated.
- **Favourite and scheduled:** turn on Favourite, select a daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or custom schedule, then save.
- **Scheduled only:** choose a schedule with Favourite off, as before.

A small filled star beside the **Repeat** field name shows that the template is a favourite. There is no extra favourite subtitle; schedule details remain in the existing helper below the field when repetition is enabled. The switch controls automatic repetition and stays off for favourite-only templates. Switching repetition off keeps the favourite mark. End conditions (never, date or occurrence count) appear only with a schedule, along with a next-transaction date control where supported. Changes are saved only when you save the transaction form.

**Availability and Pro:** Repeat is not offered when adding receipt items or a transaction from a template, or when editing a transaction already linked to a template. For linked transactions, edit the template from Recurring Transactions instead. All saved templates, including favourite-only and inactive templates, share the existing free limit of five; Pro allows unlimited templates. At the limit, tapping the Pro-marked Repeat field opens the upgrade page.

Open **Recurring Transactions → Favourites** to use saved favourites. This is the first filter and opens by default when favourites exist; otherwise All opens. Drag row handles to save a manual order, or tap a row for Add Transaction, Add to Favourites or Remove from Favourites, Edit, and Delete. See [Recurring Transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring) for detailed steps.

---

## Quick Entry Features

### Search History Button

At the bottom center of the screen, a floating search button opens Transaction History Search:
- Search through your past transactions
- Select a previous transaction to copy its details (category, description, amount, contact, tags)
- Great for quickly entering similar transactions

### Smart Suggestions

The app learns from your habits and suggests:
- **Contacts** you frequently use with the selected category
- **Descriptions** you've used before
- **Accounts** you typically use with each category

Account suggestions are limited to accounts in your current main currency.

#### Manage notes and description suggestions

On Add Transaction, Edit Transaction, and the receipt item form, long-press a description suggestion below the Description field to open a bottom sheet:
- **Hide this suggestion** hides that exact description in the selected category.
- **Hide all suggestions in this category** hides every description currently suggested for that category, including suggestions beyond the visible chips or excluded by the text you have typed. The category name appears below the action. Other categories are unaffected. New descriptions can still appear later; using an already hidden description again does not unhide it.
- **Manage notes** opens a page for the selected category, with the category name in the app bar.

When a category is selected and the Description field is empty (or contains only spaces), tap the three-dot button on its right to open the same menu without **Hide this suggestion**, even when no chips remain. The button is hidden when no category is selected or when you enter a note. The document icon on the left is decorative and has no long-press action. There is no additional settings item.

Hiding takes effect immediately, without a confirmation dialog. It does not change the current Description field or any saved transaction notes. You can still type hidden descriptions manually. Hidden choices are remembered across app launches and apply to both Add and Edit Transaction.

When opened from a receipt item, the same controls also include notes from items already added to that receipt; see [Receipt descriptions](https://budgetum.app/help/receipts#description) for draft-note behavior.

**Manage notes** starts on the **Visible** tab, showing each distinct, nonempty description used by transactions in the category that has not been hidden. Repeated transaction descriptions appear only once. The **Hidden** tab shows descriptions hidden in that category. Rows show only the description and its action icon:
- On **Visible**, tap the hide (crossed-out eye) icon to hide that description. It leaves Visible and becomes available in Hidden.
- On **Hidden**, tap the restore icon to unhide the description. It leaves Hidden and returns to Visible if a transaction in the category still uses it.
- Tapping the description or the rest of the row does nothing. Neither action inserts text into the transaction form or edits saved notes.

Tap the search icon at the top right to expand **Search notes** inside the app bar. Search filters descriptions in the current tab (case-insensitive), across the entire category, including records not yet loaded. Switching tabs keeps the search text. Tap the search-off icon in the app bar to close search and clear the filter.

Each tab initially loads up to 100 descriptions, sorted by description. Scroll to the bottom and tap **Load more** to load the next 100; the button disappears when every matching result is loaded. Changing or closing search, or switching tabs, starts again with the first 100 results.

Tap the three-dot button at the top right for bulk actions:
- On **Visible**, **Hide all (N)** hides every visible description in the category. With a nonempty search, **Hide filtered (N)** hides only matching descriptions.
- On **Hidden**, **Restore all (N)** restores every hidden description in the category. With a nonempty search, **Restore filtered (N)** restores only matching descriptions.

N is the complete matching record count, not the number of loaded rows or transactions. For example, searching “coffee” on Hidden and selecting **Restore filtered (105)** restores all 105 matching descriptions even if only 100 are loaded. Bulk actions run immediately without confirmation; other categories and saved transaction notes are unchanged. Search text and the selected tab remain in place. The bulk action is disabled when its count is zero. The three-dot and row action buttons are disabled while results load or an action is running; search and tab switching are disabled while a hide or restore is running.

The page shows a loading spinner while opening or changing filters, **No visible notes** or **No hidden suggestions** when the current tab has no records, or **No matching suggestions** when records exist in that tab but none match the search. Use Back to return to the transaction form; entered values are preserved and suggestions are refreshed. A restored suggestion appears when the category and typed text match, subject to the usual limit of ten visible chips. To manage another category, return to the form, select that category, and open **Manage notes** again.


---

## Saving Transactions

### Single Save Mode
When you open Add Transaction from a category tap:
- Tap the checkmark (✓) to save and close
- The transaction is saved and you return to the previous screen

### Multi-Entry Mode
When you open Add Transaction from the main + button:
- Tap the checkmark (✓) to save
- A "Transaction added" confirmation appears
- The form clears so you can quickly add another transaction
- The category stays selected for faster entry of multiple items in the same category

---

## Editing Transactions

### Accessing Edit Transaction

Open the Edit Transaction screen by:
- Tapping any transaction in your transaction list
- Tapping "Edit" from a transaction's options menu

### What You Can Change

All fields can be edited:
- Amount and date
- Category
- Account(s)
- Contact
- Description
- Tags
- Recurring settings (for transactions not yet linked to a recurring template)

### Edit Screen Notes

- **Contact and tags:** The contact and tags fields are always visible when editing (they are not hidden by the "Show contact on transaction creation" or "Show tags on transaction creation" settings).
- **Quick suggestions:** Description suggestion chips appear when editing, same as on Add. Recently used contact and account chips are only shown on the Add Transaction screen.
- **Foreign-currency transactions:** If the transaction uses a foreign-currency account, edit shows the saved budget amount and the saved Debited/Credited account amount. Changing either amount updates that stored value; Budgetum does not rewrite historical amounts from a live rate.
- **Combined transactions (transfers):** When editing a combined transaction, account selection is limited to accounts in your app's current currency. Different-currency transfers can be created on the Add screen; when editing, you can still change amounts but the account picker will only offer accounts in the current currency.
- **Receipt lines:** The amount is the unit price, and an **Items Count** field sits beside it. Budgets and the account use unit price × count. Changing the count updates only this line. Duplicate copies the unit price into a new transaction dated today; the copy is not part of the receipt and its count is 1. Account selection stays on the main currency.

### Also update recurring template amount

When editing a transaction that is linked to a recurring template, and you change the budget amount (or the foreign-currency Debited/Credited amount), a checkbox appears:

- **Also update recurring template amount**

Leave it off to change only this occurrence. Check it to also write the new amount(s) back to the recurring template so future generated occurrences use the updated template amount. The same checkbox appears when editing a linked transfer or balance adjustment from their edit screens.

### Additional Edit Options

The three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right provides extra options:

**Change to income** / **Change to expense:**
- Switches the transaction between income and expense
- The title area shows an **Income** or **Expense** badge for the current type; this menu is how you change it (there is no type toggle on Edit)
- Hidden for receipt-linked items
- Switching type swaps the from and to accounts
- If you switch to expense and the current category is an income category, the category is cleared and you must select a category before saving
- Switching to income keeps an expense category (for refunds or money returned to a spending category)
- The **Also update recurring template amount** checkbox is hidden while the edited type differs from the linked template’s type

**Edit receipt:**
- Shown when this transaction belongs to a receipt
- Opens that receipt with all of its items, including items that are not this line
- When you leave the receipt, you return to the list, not this transaction editor

**Transform to Receipt:**
- Converts a single expense transaction into a multi-item receipt
- Useful when you realize a transaction should be split across multiple categories
- Only available for expense transactions that are not already part of a receipt and are not combined transfers (the source account, if any, must also use your main currency)

**Duplicate:**
- Creates a copy of the transaction with today's date
- All other details are preserved
- Opens as a new Add Transaction screen with the values pre-filled

**Delete:**
- Permanently removes the transaction
- You'll be asked to confirm before deletion
- This action cannot be undone

### Update Similar Transactions

When you change a description, a checkbox may appear:

**"Update X similar transactions"**
- If you have other transactions with the same original description
- Check this box to update all of them to the new description
- Useful for fixing typos or improving consistency

---

## Combined Transactions (Transfer + Budget)

For advanced tracking, you can create a combined transaction that:
1. Records a budget transaction (expense or income to a category)
2. Records an account transfer at the same time

### How to Enable

1. Select an account in the "From Account" field
2. Tap the swap icon (↔) next to the account field
3. A second account field appears for the transfer destination

### Transfer Amount

When **creating** a combined transaction, you can select accounts with different currencies:
- You can enter different amounts for each side
- The number picker may offer a market-rate quick suggestion between the two account currencies
- This handles exchange rate differences without storing a permanent rate table

When **editing** an existing transaction, account selection is limited to your app's current currency (see "Edit Screen Notes" under Editing Transactions).

### When to Use

Combined transactions are helpful when:
- You receive income into one of your accounts and want to record the transfer
- You record savings as an expense and transfer to your savings account
- You want to track both the category spending and the money movement

---

## Tips for Adding Transactions

1. **Add transactions promptly** - Record expenses right after they happen while details are fresh

2. **Use the search feature** - The history search helps you quickly find and copy past transactions

3. **Be consistent with descriptions** - Use similar descriptions for similar transactions to make searching easier

4. **Assign contacts** - Linking transactions to contacts helps you analyze spending by store or person

5. **Use tags for special tracking** - Tags let you track things across categories (like vacation expenses)

6. **Check the date** - Make sure the date is correct, especially when entering transactions from receipts or statements

7. **Set up recurring transactions** - Save time by setting up repeating bills and income once

8. **Use quick-select chips** - The suggestion chips below fields speed up entry significantly

9. **Review before saving** - Double-check the amount and category before tapping save

10. **Foreign-currency spending** - For a USD card with a UAH budget (for example), enter the real card charge as Debited/Credited and the budget value as Amount so reports stay in your main currency

---

# Receipts

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/receipts

Receipts in Budgetum let you record multiple purchases from a single shopping trip or invoice as individual transactions. Instead of creating one transaction for your entire grocery bill, you can split it into categories like groceries, household supplies, and snacks—giving you more accurate insights into where your money actually goes.

## Accessing the Add Receipt Screen

You can open the Add Receipt screen by:
- Opening **Add Transaction** in expense mode and tapping the split icon next to the **Category** field
- Using the **Add Receipt** option from an account's transaction view
- Converting an existing transaction to a receipt via the Edit Transaction menu

When opened from Add Transaction, Budgetum carries over the selected account, date, contact, and any amount already typed as the receipt total. A selected category is used only to filter store suggestions; it is not applied to receipt items.

---

## How Receipts Work

A receipt in Budgetum is a collection of items that all share the same:
- **Date** - When the purchase happened
- **Account** - Which account you paid from
- **Contact** - The store or business where you shopped

Each item within the receipt can have its own:
- **Amount** - How much that item cost
- **Category** - Which budget category it belongs to
- **Description** - What the item was
- **Tags** - Additional labels for organization

This lets you accurately categorize a single shopping trip across multiple budget categories.

---

## Add Receipt Screen Layout

### Total and Date Row

At the top of the form:

**Total Field:**
- Enter the total amount from your receipt
- Tap to open the calculator-style number picker
- This is the target amount—your item totals should match this
- The app will alert you if your items don't add up to the total

**Date Field:**
- Shows the receipt date
- Tap to open the date picker
- All items on this receipt will use this date

---

### Account Selection

**From Account Field:**
- Select which account you paid from
- Tap to open the account picker (only accounts in your current main currency are available; foreign-currency accounts cannot be used on receipts)
- Use the clear button (×) to clear the selection
- Quick-select chips appear below showing recently used accounts in your current main currency (chips may be hidden when you have only one default account and it is already selected)

This account will be applied to all items on the receipt. The account section is only shown when you have at least one active account.

---

### Contact Selection

**"Paid to" (Payment Recipient) Field:**
- Select the store or business where you made the purchase
- Tap to open the contact picker, or tap a chip to select a recent contact (tap again to clear)
- Quick-select chips show recently used contacts. When Add Receipt was opened from Add Transaction with a category selected, the chips show contacts recently used with that category. Opening the contact picker uses the same category for its suggestions.

This contact will be applied to all items on the receipt.

**Note:** This field only appears if you have the "Show contact on transaction creation" setting enabled.

---

### Items List

Below the header fields, you'll see:

**"Add Item" Button:**
- Tap to add a new item to the receipt
- Opens the Add Receipt Item screen

**Items Card:**
- Lists all items you've added
- Each item shows:
  - Category name and icon
  - Description (if provided)
  - Tags (if assigned)
  - Quantity badge (if more than 1)
  - Amount in the category's color
- Tap any item to edit it

---

### Balance Indicator

At the bottom of the screen, a colored bar appears when your items don't match the total:

**"Remaining: $XX.XX" (Blue)**
- Your items total less than the receipt total
- The remaining amount needs to be assigned to items
- Tap "Fix" to quickly add an item for the remaining amount

**"Excess: $XX.XX" (Red)**
- Your items total more than the receipt total
- You've added more than the receipt amount
- Tap "Fix" to automatically adjust the total to match your items

The save button only appears when your items exactly match the receipt total.

**Closing the screen:** Tap the close (×) button to leave. If the total, date, account, contact, or items differ from when you opened the receipt, the app asks whether to discard your changes. An unchanged receipt closes immediately.

---

## Adding Receipt Items

When you tap "Add Item", the Add Receipt Item screen opens with these fields:

### Amount and Count Row

**Amount Field:**
- The price of this item
- Tap to open the calculator number picker
- Enter the unit price if buying multiples

**Items Count Field:**
- How many of this item you bought
- Defaults to 1
- The field is read-only; tap it to open the Number Picker (titled **Items Count**)
- Must be a positive whole number (1, 2, 3, …). You cannot type a count freely, and decimals or zero are rejected
- Increase for multiples (e.g., 3 bottles of water)
- The total for this line will be amount × count

**Price Suggestions:**
When you have a category (or description) entered and have more than one previous price for similar transactions, price chips appear below the amount field. Tap a chip to quickly select that price.

---

### Category

**Category Field:**
- Select which budget category this item belongs to
- Only expense categories are shown (receipts are for expenses)
- The category's icon and color help you identify it
- If you've already added items, the last-used category is remembered

---

### Description

**Description Field:**
- Describe what this item is
- Examples: "Milk 2%", "Birthday candles", "Paper towels"
- Helps you remember what the purchase was for
- Supports multiple lines for longer notes

**Description Suggestions:**
After you select a category, up to ten chips appear below showing descriptions from saved transactions and items already added to the current receipt in that category, excluding hidden notes. The list is filtered as you type. Tap anywhere inside a chip, including the space around its text, to fill the Description field and refresh suggested prices.

When adding or editing a receipt item, long-press a description chip to open the usual bottom sheet:
- **Hide this suggestion** hides that exact note in this category.
- **Hide all suggestions in this category** hides all current notes in the category, including notes from other unsaved items in this receipt and notes beyond the visible chips. It does not use the text currently typed in the Description field as a filter.
- **Manage notes** opens the selected category’s notes page.

When a category is selected and the Description field is empty (or contains only spaces), tap its right-hand three-dot button to open the same menu without **Hide this suggestion**. This remains available after all chips are hidden. The button is hidden when no category is selected or when you enter a note. The document icon on the left is decorative and has no long-press action.

**Manage notes** has **Visible** and **Hidden** toggles and starts on Visible. Visible includes distinct notes from saved transactions and other items already added to this receipt; duplicates appear only once. Hidden includes the category’s hidden notes. The category name appears in the app bar. Tap the hide icon on a Visible row or the restore icon on a Hidden row; tapping the row text does nothing. Restoring a draft-only note returns it to Visible while it is still present in this receipt.

Use the search icon in the app bar to open **Search notes**. It searches the current view across all records, including unloaded ones. Switching Visible/Hidden keeps the search text; the search-off icon clears it. Notes load in batches of 100 with **Load more** at the bottom. Switching views or changing search returns to the first batch.

The three-dot menu offers **Hide all (N)** on Visible and **Restore all (N)** on Hidden. With a nonempty search, these become **Hide filtered (N)** and **Restore filtered (N)**. N counts all matching distinct notes, including unloaded notes and, on Visible, draft receipt notes. Actions run immediately without confirmation and affect only this category. Zero-count actions are disabled; loading or an ongoing action temporarily disables controls.

Use Back to return to the receipt item. Its entered description, amount, quantity, category, and tags are preserved, and suggestion chips refresh. Hiding or restoring never edits saved transaction notes or receipt items. Hidden choices are shared with Add/Edit Transaction and remain saved even if you cancel the receipt; a hidden draft-only note can be restored from Hidden later, but appears in Visible only if a saved transaction or the current receipt still contains it. Price suggestions and receipt history search remain available independently of hidden description chips. See [Manage notes and description suggestions](https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction#manage-notes-and-description-suggestions) for empty states and detailed shared controls.

---

### Tags

**Tags Field:**
- Add labels to this specific item
- Useful for tracking specific purposes (e.g., "Party supplies")
- Multiple tags can be selected

**Tag Suggestions:**
Chips show your recently used tags for quick selection.

**Note:** The tags field only appears if you have the "Show tags on transaction creation" setting enabled.

---

### Saving Items

**Add Another (✓ button):**
- When adding a new item, tap the checkmark to save and add another
- The form clears but keeps your category (and tags) selected for the next item
- A confirmation message appears briefly
- Continue adding items until you've entered everything

**Save Edit:**
- When editing an existing item, tap the checkmark to save changes
- You return to the receipt screen

**Delete (trash icon):**
- Only appears when editing an existing item
- Removes the item from the receipt

### Remaining / excess bar (adding an item)

When you are **adding** a new item (not editing one) and the receipt has a total greater than zero, a bar at the bottom of the item screen shows how the already-added items compare with that total:

**Remaining: $XX.XX**
- The added items total less than the receipt total
- Tap **Add remaining** to fill the amount with the leftover and set **Items Count** to 1. You still choose a category (and other fields) and save the item with the checkmark.

**Excess: $XX.XX**
- The added items total more than the receipt total
- No action button is shown on this bar

**Save receipt**
- Appears on the bar when the added items already match the receipt total exactly
- Saves the whole receipt from the item screen using the items already added; it does not add the item you are currently typing
- After a successful save, you leave the receipt

This bar is hidden when you are editing an existing item, or when the receipt has no total yet.

---

### Search History

At the bottom of the Add Receipt Item screen, a floating search button opens the Receipt History Search:

**How it works:**
- Search through your past transactions
- Find items you've purchased before
- Select a result to copy its category, description, and amount
- Great for items you buy regularly

When you have a contact selected on the receipt, the search prioritizes transactions with that contact, making it easy to find items you've bought at that store before.

---

## Editing, Duplicating, and Deleting a Saved Receipt

Long-press a receipt group in a transaction list to open **Edit**, **Duplicate**, and **Delete**. These actions are also available from the receipt's transaction group page.

Long-press a single receipt item, including on category, section, contact, and tag lists where items are not grouped, and choose **Edit receipt**. The same action is in the three-dot menu on Edit Transaction for that item. It opens the receipt with all of its items. From Edit Transaction, leaving the receipt returns you to the list.

**Edit** opens the same form used to create a receipt, with all its items loaded even when the transaction list is filtered. Change the date, account, contact, or individual items; add items, remove items, or change quantities. The item total must match the receipt total before saving.

Changes stay in the form until you save. Saving updates the receipt and account balances together, preserving existing transaction identities where possible. Closing with no changes leaves immediately. If you changed the receipt, the app asks before discarding. Cancelling leaves the saved receipt untouched.

**Duplicate** opens a new receipt draft with the original items and today's date. **Delete** asks for confirmation before removing the entire receipt and all its transactions.

---

## Editing Receipt Items

Tap any item in the items list to:
- Change its amount, count, category, description, or tags
- Delete the item from the receipt

Changes take effect immediately when you save.

---

## Saving the Receipt

The save button (✓) in the top-right corner only appears when:
- You have at least one item
- Your items' total exactly matches the receipt total

**When you save:**
- Each item line becomes one transaction. Its amount is the line total (unit price × count), and the count is stored on that transaction
- Identical lines stay separate. Count is not combined across lines
- All transactions share the same date, account, and contact
- Each transaction goes to its respective category
- The items are linked together as a receipt group

---

## Converting a Transaction to a Receipt

If you've already recorded a single transaction but want to split it:

1. Open the transaction for editing
2. Tap the three-dot menu (⋮)
3. Select "Transform to Receipt"
4. The receipt screen opens with the amount and contact pre-filled
5. Add individual items to break down the purchase
6. The original transaction is replaced when you save

**Use this when:**
- You recorded a quick total but want more detail later
- You realize a purchase spans multiple categories
- You have time to properly categorize a shopping trip

---

## Viewing Receipt History

Receipts appear in your transaction history like regular transactions, but:
- On Transactions, account lists, and sets, items from the same receipt on the same day are grouped together. If they all use one category, the group title is that category name with a receipt icon after it. If they use different categories, the group title is Receipt and the icon on the left is the receipt icon.
- Category, section, contact, tag, and similar lists show each item on its own. A receipt icon after the category name (or after the description, when the category name is hidden) means that line belongs to a receipt.
- The receipt's total contact badge shows on all items
- Each item shows its category and line total. When the count is greater than 1, the line also shows ×N

**Tip:** Tap any receipt item to view and edit just that item, or view the contact to see all transactions at that store.

---

## Tips for Using Receipts

1. **Enter the total first** - Start with the receipt total so you know when you've accounted for everything

2. **Use the search feature** - The history search finds items you've bought before, saving time on repeat purchases

3. **Keep it simple** - You don't need to itemize everything; group small similar items together

4. **Use descriptions** - Brief descriptions like "produce" or "cleaning supplies" help you remember later

5. **Check your math** - The balance indicator helps ensure you don't miss or double-count items

6. **Set the contact** - Linking to a store lets you analyze spending by location over time

7. **Add items as you go** - You can add items, return to the receipt, and add more without losing progress

8. **Use the count field** - For multiples of the same item at the same price, use count instead of adding separate items

9. **Let suggestions help** - The price and description suggestions from your history speed up entry significantly

---

## Example: Grocery Store Receipt

Here's how you might enter a grocery store receipt:

**Receipt header:** Total $87.54, date today, account Checking Account, contact Supermart.

**Items you add:**

- **Groceries** — Fruits and vegetables, $23.45 × 1  
- **Groceries** — Dairy (milk 2%), $6.50 × 2 → $13.00  
- **Groceries** — Meat, $28.50 × 1  
- **Household** — Paper products, $8.99 × 1  
- **Health** — Vitamins, $13.60 × 1  

The milk line uses count 2 so you enter one line (price × 2) instead of two separate lines. Your item total matches the receipt total, so the save button appears. When you save, you get **five** transactions, one per line. The milk transaction is $13.00 with count 2, shown as ×2 in the receipt's transaction list. The others are one each at their line amount. All share the same date, account, and contact, each in its category.

---

# Recurring transactions

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/recurring

The Recurring Transactions Screen manages saved transaction templates: scheduled subscriptions, bills and income, plus favourites you reuse manually. A template can be a favourite, have an automatic repeat schedule, or both. Favourites use the same transaction details as other templates; there is no separate template-name field.

## Accessing the Recurring Screen

You can access the Recurring Transactions Screen by:
- Tapping the repeat icon (↻) in the top bar of the Transactions screen
- Going to **More → Advanced Features → Recurring Transactions**

---

## Understanding Recurring Transactions

Templates with an active repeat schedule automatically create transactions on that schedule. Marking a template as **Favourite** alone does not enable automatic repetition. Common examples include:

- **Subscriptions** - Netflix, Spotify, gym memberships
- **Bills** - Rent, utilities, phone bills, insurance
- **Regular Income** - Salary, freelance payments, rental income
- **Scheduled Transfers** - Regular savings transfers, investment contributions
- **Recurring Fees** - Bank fees, service charges

Scheduled templates generate transactions on their scheduled dates. Favourite-only templates wait for you to choose **Add Transaction** from their options.

---

## Screen Layout

### Filter Bar

At the top of the screen, you'll find filter buttons to quickly narrow down which recurring transactions to display:

- **Favourites** - The first filter; shows all templates marked as Favourite, whether scheduled or not, in your saved manual order
- **All** - Shows all templates (active and inactive, including favourites)
- **Day** - Only templates that repeat daily
- **Week** - Only templates that repeat weekly
- **Month** - Only templates that repeat monthly
- **Year** - Only templates that repeat yearly
- **Not Active** - Templates that have been saved but don't have an active recurrence schedule

When you open this screen, **Favourites** is selected if at least one favourite exists; otherwise **All** is selected. Tap any filter to switch the view. The selected filter is highlighted. Updates while the screen is open preserve your chosen filter. A scheduled favourite also appears in All and its matching frequency filter; a favourite without a schedule also appears in All and Not Active.

### Search

Tap the search icon in the top right corner to find specific recurring transactions (tap again to close search). You can search by:

- Template description or notes
- Category name
- Budget section name
- Amount
- Account name (source or destination)
- Contact name
- Tags
- Recurrence pattern (e.g., "monthly", "weekly")

When searching, matching templates are displayed while non-matching ones are hidden.

### Pro Version Banner

If you're using the free version of Budgetum, you'll see a banner at the top of the list indicating that the free tier is limited to 5 recurring transaction templates. The banner is hidden while search is open or when a search query is active. Upgrade to Pro for unlimited templates. Favourite-only, scheduled and inactive templates all count toward the same five-template free limit. A template that is both a favourite and scheduled counts once. Favourites do not receive a separate free allowance. At the limit, the Repeat field for creating a new template shows a Pro badge and opens the upgrade page; existing templates remain editable.

---

## Recurring Templates List

### Favourites List and Manual Order

Favourites appear as a flat list without date groups. Drag the small dotted grip at the left of a row to move it; the new order is saved immediately and remains after reopening the app. A template you newly mark as a favourite is added at the end of the list. Reordering is available only in Favourites. When a search query is entered, the drag handles are hidden; clear the query to reorder again. If saving the order fails, an error message appears and the list reloads its saved order.

Tap a favourite anywhere in its main row to open the same options as other templates: **Add Transaction**, **Remove from Favourites**, **Edit**, and **Delete**. Reordering does not change its schedule or transaction details. Backups preserve favourite marks and saved ordering.

### Active Templates (Grouped by Next Date)

Outside the Favourites filter, active recurring templates are organized by their next scheduled occurrence date. Each date group shows:

- **Calendar icon and date** - When the next occurrence will happen (displayed in a friendly format like "Today", "Tomorrow", "Monday", or the full date)
- **Total amount** - The net amount for that date: income minus expenses. It shows a "+" when income is larger (for example, a $3,200 paycheck and $1,850 rent on the same day show **+$1,350**) and no sign when expenses are larger. Transfers and balance adjustments are not counted, and the total is hidden when the net is zero

Below each date header, you'll see the individual templates grouped under that date.

### Template Display

Each recurring template shows the following information:

**Main Row:**
- **Category icon** (on the left) - The icon of the budget section this template belongs to
- **Category or title** - The name of the category, or for transfers and balance adjustments, a descriptive title. Outside the Favourites filter, a filled star after the name means the template is a favourite. The star is hidden on Favourites, where every row is already a favourite
- **Amount** (on the right) - The template amount with color coding:
  - "+" prefix and income color = Income (uses your budget's Income section color)
  - Section color = Expenses (matches the category's budget section color)

**Additional Details (when applicable):**
- **Contact badge** - Shows which person or business this recurring transaction involves
- **Account badge** - Shows which account is used
- **Description** - Any notes you added to the template
- **Tags** - Hashtags for additional categorization (shown as #tagname)
- **Recurrence label** - Shown only for active schedules. Inactive templates, including favourites without a schedule, have no recurrence label. A description of the active schedule (e.g., "Every month", "Every 2 weeks", "Every Monday", "1st and 15th of the month")

### Inactive Templates Section

Templates that have been saved without an active recurrence schedule appear in two ways:

- **When "Not Active" is selected** – Only inactive templates are shown (no date groups).
- **When "All" is selected** – Active templates appear first, grouped by next date; inactive templates are listed at the bottom under a "Not Active" header. Frequency filters (Day, Week, Month, Year) show active schedules only.
- **When "Favourites" is selected** – Inactive favourites appear alongside scheduled favourites in your manual order.

These are useful for:

- Templates you've paused temporarily
- One-time templates you might want to reactivate later
- Drafts you haven't fully configured yet

The inactive section has a "Not Active" header and displays templates with a different visual styling.

---

## Template Types

### Regular Recurring Transactions

Standard income or expense templates linked to a budget category. These are the most common type—things like your monthly rent, weekly grocery budget, or salary.

### Recurring Transfers

Templates for regular money movement between your accounts. Transfer templates show:
- A swap icon (↔) indicating a transfer
- The source and destination accounts with an arrow between them
- The transfer amount

Common uses: monthly savings transfers, regular investment contributions, credit card payments.

### Recurring Balance Adjustments

Templates for regular balance corrections. These show:
- "Balance Increase" or "Balance Decrease" as the title
- A plus or minus icon indicating the adjustment direction
- The affected account

Common uses: recurring bank fees, regular interest payments, scheduled adjustments.

---

## Working with Templates

### Quick access from Budget and Transactions

When Favourites is selected and the list is not empty, a small hint below the filters explains: **Hold + on Budget or Transactions to add from favourites.** Tap its **×** button to dismiss it. The hint also disappears after you first open the favourites shortcut sheet, even if you close that sheet without adding a transaction. This is remembered after restarting the app. **More → Reset Tutorial** restores the hint, including after you have already used the shortcut. The hint is not shown in other filters or when there are no matching favourites.

Long-press the **+** button at the bottom center to open **Favourites**. This shortcut is available only when at least one favourite template exists; a normal tap still opens a blank Add Transaction form. The scrollable bottom sheet lists all favourites in the order saved on Recurring Transactions, including favourites with a repeat schedule. A star appears beside the Favourites title. Favourites appear directly on the sheet background as tappable rows separated by subtle dividers. Repeat schedule text is hidden in this shortcut; view schedules on Recurring Transactions. Tap anywhere on a row to close the sheet and open a new transaction prefilled from that template, using today’s date. Transfers and balance adjustments open their corresponding forms. Review the details and save; opening a favourite does not save a transaction. If its amount is 0, the number picker opens automatically (the source-account amount for transfers). Dismiss the picker to return to the form, or dismiss the favourites sheet to return to the screen without adding anything. Add or remove favourites, edit, delete, and reorder them on [Recurring Transactions](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring); those controls are not shown in this shortcut.

This shortcut uses the existing favourites and does not require a separate Pro upgrade. Creating templates remains subject to the shared free limit described above. Creating a manual transaction from a scheduled favourite does not change its repeat schedule. Zero-amount templates also open the number picker when you choose **Add Transaction** from this screen.

### Template options

**Tap a recurring template** in the list to open an options sheet with:
- **Add Transaction** — create a one-off transaction prefilled from the template (category, amount, accounts, contact and tags where applicable), using today’s date. Review or change the details and save to create the transaction. The new transaction stays associated with the template for history and reporting.
- **Add to Favourites** or **Remove from Favourites** — mark or unmark the template immediately. The label matches its current state. This does not delete the template or change its schedule, amount, accounts, or other details. A newly added favourite appears at the end of the list. Adding it again after you remove it also places it at the end. The list updates as soon as you choose the option.
- **Edit** — open the Edit Template screen
- **Delete** — remove the template (existing transactions created from it are kept)

Opening the options sheet does not create a transaction. The **Add Transaction** subtitle explains that it creates a transaction from the template. Choosing **Add to Favourites** or **Remove from Favourites** closes the sheet and saves that change; you do not need to open Edit or save the template again.

### Editing a Template

From the options sheet, choose **Edit** to open **Edit Template**.

For regular income or expense templates, the title area shows an **Income** or **Expense** badge. Transfers and balance-adjustment templates do not show this badge.

The three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right includes:

**Change to income** / **Change to expense:**
- Switches the template between income and expense
- Not shown for transfer or balance-adjustment templates
- Switching type swaps the from and to accounts
- If you switch to expense and the current category is an income category, the category is cleared and you must select a category before saving

**Delete** is also in this menu (see [Deleting a Template](https://budgetum.app/help/recurring#deleting-a-template)).

**Transaction Details:**
- **Amount and Start Date** - The template budget amount and when the recurrence begins
- **Category** - The budget category (for regular transactions)
- **Accounts** - Source and/or destination accounts
- **Foreign-currency amounts** - If the primary account uses a currency different from the app's main currency, an extra **Debited** / **Credited** field appears for the account-side amount (same idea as Add/Edit Transaction). Occurrences copy both the budget amount and the account amount; no live rate lookup runs during generation
- **Update from an occurrence** - When you edit a transaction already linked to this template and change its amount, Edit Transaction can offer **Also update recurring template amount** so future occurrences pick up the new template amount → [Add/Edit Transaction](https://budgetum.app/help/add-transaction)
- **Contact** - The person or business involved
- **Description** - Notes about this recurring transaction
- **Tags** - Any tags for organization

**Recurrence Settings:**
- **Favourite** - From the template options, choose **Add to Favourites** or **Remove from Favourites**. That change is saved immediately and does not delete the template or change its schedule. You can also open Repeat while editing and turn Favourite on or off; that choice is saved when you save the template.
- **Recurrence pattern** - How often and when the template repeats
- Options include: daily, weekly, monthly, yearly, or custom schedules
- You can set specific days of the week, days of the month, or create complex patterns

**Transaction History:**
- Below the form, you'll see a list of actual transactions that have been created from this template
- This helps you verify that the recurring transaction is working correctly
- Tap "Show More" to load additional history

### Saving Changes

Tap the checkmark (✓) in the top right corner to save your changes. The template will be updated and future occurrences will use the new settings.

### Deleting a Template

Open the three-dot menu (⋮) in the top right and choose **Delete**. You'll be asked to confirm before the template is permanently deleted.

**Note:** Deleting a template does not delete transactions that were already created from it. Those transactions remain in your history.

---

## Recurrence Options

Budgetum supports flexible scheduling for recurring transactions:

### Common Presets
- **Daily** - Every day
- **Weekly** - Every week on the same day
- **Every 2 Weeks** - Bi-weekly
- **Monthly** - Every month on the same date
- **Yearly** - Once a year on the same date

### Custom Schedules

For more complex needs, you can create custom recurrence patterns:

- **Specific weekdays** - Every Monday and Wednesday
- **Specific days of the month** - The 1st and 15th of each month
- **Nth weekday** - The first Monday of each month, the last Friday
- **Multiple months** - Only in certain months of the year
- **Custom intervals** - Every 3 weeks, every 6 months, etc.

### Schedule Limits

You can optionally set:
- **End date** - Stop the recurrence after a specific date
- **Maximum occurrences** - Stop after a certain number of transactions

---

## Empty States

### No Recurring Transactions

If you haven't set up any recurring transactions yet, or when the current filter has no matching templates (for example, you have only inactive templates and filter by "Month"), the screen displays:
- A repeat icon
- A message indicating you have no recurring transactions

This is a great time to set up your regular bills and income!

### No Favourites

If Favourites is selected but contains no templates, the screen says: **No favourites yet. Tap a template in another filter and choose Add to Favourites.** This can happen after removing the last favourite while this filter is open. Switch to All or another filter, tap a template, and choose **Add to Favourites**. You can also mark a template as Favourite in Repeat options while editing it. On the next visit with no favourites, All opens by default.

### No Search Results

When searching, if no templates match your query:
- An empty-results icon appears
- A message indicates no results were found

Try adjusting your search terms or clearing the search.

---

## Creating Recurring Transactions

To save a favourite, a schedule, or both:

1. Open Add Transaction and fill in its details, or edit a transaction that is not already linked to a template. The same Repeat control is available in transfer and balance-adjustment forms when template creation is allowed.
2. Tap **Repeat** (the repeat icon/row, its arrow, or its switch when off) to open the options page.
3. Turn on the **Favourite** switch at the top. When no favourite templates are saved, a small, muted helper beneath the switch explains that favourites let you quickly add transactions without a repeat schedule. It is hidden when you open Repeat with at least one saved favourite. Turning it on or off keeps the options page open and retains the choice in the parent form.
4. For a favourite without a schedule, leave **Do not repeat** selected and use Back, or tap **Do not repeat** to return. For a scheduled favourite, select a repeat preset: the page returns immediately with both choices. **Custom** opens custom schedule settings; applying them also returns with the favourite mark preserved.
5. Back in the form, a small filled star beside the **Repeat** field name identifies a favourite. There is no extra favourite subtitle; the existing schedule helper remains below the field when repetition is enabled. The switch represents automatic repetition: it stays off for favourite-only templates. Turning it off preserves the favourite mark but disables repetition. End and next-transaction controls are shown only when a schedule is enabled (the next-date control is available in forms that support it).
6. Save the transaction or, when editing a template, tap the top-right checkmark. Returning from Repeat only updates the form; leaving the parent form without saving does not save those changes.

The template appears in Favourites if marked. Scheduled templates also appear in their frequency filter. To mark an existing template, tap it in any filter and choose **Add to Favourites**. To remove it, tap it and choose **Remove from Favourites**. Either choice is saved immediately; the template remains in All, and any active schedule continues. You can still change the favourite mark from **Edit** → Repeat, which is saved when you save the template.

Repeat is unavailable when adding receipt items or creating a transaction from a template, and is hidden when editing a transaction already linked to a template. Use **Edit** on the template itself to change its favourite mark or schedule. Favourite templates share the existing Pro limits described above.

---

## How Recurring Transactions Work

### Automatic Generation

Budgetum automatically generates transactions from your templates based on their schedule:

1. The template tracks the "next occurrence" date
2. When that date arrives (or passes), a planned transaction is created and appears in your Transactions list
3. The transaction appears on your budget and in the Transactions list, and is marked as requiring confirmation: you can approve it (to clear the flag), edit and approve, or delete it. After you approve, account balances are updated to reflect the transaction.
4. After each occurrence, the next date is calculated based on your recurrence pattern

### Confirmation Required Block

Transactions generated from recurring templates (and any other planned transactions that require confirmation) appear in the **Confirmation Required** block at the top of the Transactions screen. They are also included in your budget totals and shown on the Budget screen. The block can be expanded or collapsed. From there you can approve a transaction (to clear the confirmation flag), edit it and then approve, or delete it. After you approve, account balances are updated to reflect the transaction.

### Missed Occurrences

If you don't open the app for a while, Budgetum catches up by generating any missed occurrences. Past-due recurring transactions will appear in your history with their correct dates.

---

## Tips for Managing Recurring Transactions

1. **Set up all your bills** - Enter your rent, utilities, subscriptions, and regular expenses so nothing gets forgotten

2. **Include regular income** - Add your salary, freelance payments, or other regular income sources

3. **Use descriptive names** - Add descriptions to templates so you remember what each one is for (e.g., "Netflix subscription", "Monthly gym fee")

4. **Review regularly** - Check the Recurring screen periodically to update canceled subscriptions or changed amounts

5. **Use the filters** - If you have many recurring items, use the frequency filters to focus on specific types

6. **Check transaction history** - Use the history in the edit screen to verify that transactions are being created correctly

7. **Set appropriate accounts** - Link each recurring transaction to the correct account so your balances stay accurate

8. **Use contacts** - Add contacts to recurring transactions to track who you pay or receive money from regularly

9. **Foreign-currency templates** - For subscriptions charged in another currency, set both the budget amount and the account Debited/Credited amount on the template so generated occurrences stay correct without needing the network

10. **Pause instead of delete** - If you temporarily stop a subscription, you can remove the recurrence without deleting the template, making it easy to reactivate later

11. **Use the Confirmation Required block** - Recurring-generated transactions appear there until you approve them; you can edit the amount (or other details) before confirming if needed

---

# Day view

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/day-view

The Day Transactions Screen provides a focused view of your transactions for a specific day, with an integrated calendar for easy navigation between dates. This screen helps you review daily spending patterns and see exactly what happened on any given day.

## Accessing the Day Transactions Screen

You can access the Day Transactions Screen by:
- **Main Transactions screen** — Tapping the calendar icon in the app bar
- **Account, category, or other entity** — When viewing transactions for an account, category, section, contact, or tag, tapping the calendar icon in the period bar (the bar below the header that shows the date range) opens the Day Transactions Screen for that same entity

---

## Screen Layout

### Top Bar (Header)

The top bar stays visible while you scroll. It displays the currently selected date and provides quick navigation controls.

**Elements:**
- **Left Arrow (<)** - Navigate to the previous day
- **Selected Date** - Shows the current date in a friendly format (e.g., "Today", "Yesterday", "Mon, Jan 20")
- **Daily Total** - Displays the net total for the selected day (income minus expenses). Shown only when the day has transactions or when in selection mode with at least one transaction selected.
- **Right Arrow (>)** - Navigate to the next day
- **Selection Mode Button** - Toggle multi-select mode for transactions (checkmark icon). Hidden for future dates.

**Actions:**
- **Tap the date or calendar icon beside it** to scroll back to the calendar at the top of the page. This preserves the selected day and any selected transactions.
- **Tap the arrows** to move forward or backward one day at a time

### Daily Total Display

When the day has transactions (or in selection mode), below the date you'll see:
- A positive total (with + prefix) when income exceeds expenses
- A negative total when expenses exceed income
- The total updates in real-time as you navigate between days
- In selection mode, the total shows the sum of only the selected transactions (for an account, the net impact on that account)

---

## Calendar View

The calendar is shown at the top of the page when you open this screen. It and the selected day’s transactions scroll together: swipe up to move past the calendar and read more transactions, or scroll back to the top to choose another date. Tapping the date or its calendar icon in the fixed header also returns to the calendar. There is no calendar hide/show toggle.

### Month Navigation

At the top of the calendar:
- **Left Arrow (<)** - Go to the previous month
- **Month and Year** - Tap to open a month/year picker for faster navigation
- **Right Arrow (>)** - Go to the next month

### Calendar Grid

A row of weekday labels (e.g. Mon, Tue, …) appears above the grid. The calendar displays only the current month’s days with the following features:

**Day Tiles:**
- Each day shows the day number
- Days with transactions display daily income (in the income color with + prefix) and expenses (in red with - prefix)
- The selected day is highlighted with a colored border and subtle background
- Today's date has a special border highlight
- Future days appear slightly faded
- Empty cells before the first day of the month are left blank (other months’ days are not shown)

**Actions:**
- **Tap any day in the current month** to select it and view its transactions
- Selecting a day updates the header, daily total, and transactions below without closing the calendar or automatically scrolling away from it. It exits selection mode and clears any selected transactions.

### Month/Year Picker

When you tap the month name in the calendar header, a picker opens allowing you to:
- Quickly jump to any month
- Navigate between years
- See which months have transaction data

---

## Transaction List

Below the calendar, you'll see all transactions for the selected day.

### Transaction Display

Each transaction shows:
- **Category icon** - Visual indicator of the transaction category
- **Category name** - The budget category this transaction belongs to
- **Amount** - The transaction amount with appropriate color coding:
  - Green with + prefix for income
  - Category section color for expenses
  
### Additional Details

Transactions may also display:
- **Receipt icon** - Shown after the category name, or after the description when that is the row title, when the transaction belongs to a receipt and is listed on its own. Grouping follows the list you opened this day from: account and set days can still fold several receipt items into one group, and that group shows the receipt icon after the category name when every item uses the same category.
- **Recurring icon (↻)** - Indicates a recurring transaction
- **Confirmation icon (?)** - Indicates confirmation is required
- **Transfer icon (↔)** - Indicates a transfer between accounts
- **Contact badge** - Shows associated person or business
- **Account badge** - Shows which account was used
- **Description** - Any notes added to the transaction
- **Tags** - Hashtags for additional categorization

### Grouped Transactions

Depending on context, transactions may be grouped by:
- **Receipt** - Multiple items from the same receipt shown together
- **Contact** - Transactions with the same person or business grouped

### Empty State

If there are no transactions for the selected day:
- A receipt icon is displayed
- A “No results found” message is shown

---

## Selection Mode

The Day Transactions Screen includes a powerful selection mode for analyzing multiple transactions at once.

### Activating Selection Mode

Tap the checkmark icon in the top-right corner of the header to enter selection mode.

### Using Selection Mode

When in selection mode:
- **Tap individual transactions** to select or deselect them
- **Tap a group header** to select or deselect all transactions in that group
- Selected transactions show a checkmark indicator
- The header total updates to show the combined total of only selected transactions

### Viewing Selected Totals

While in selection mode, the daily total in the header changes to show:
- The combined amount of all selected transactions
- This helps you quickly calculate subtotals for specific purchases or activities

### Exiting Selection Mode

Tap the checkmark icon again to exit selection mode and clear all selections.

**Note:** Selection mode is not available for future dates (dates that haven't occurred yet).

---

## Transaction Types and Actions

### Tapping Transactions

Different transaction types have different behaviors when tapped:

**Regular Transactions (Income/Expenses):**
Opens the Edit Transaction screen where you can modify all details.

**Recurring Preview Transactions:**
For transactions that are previews of upcoming recurring entries, tapping opens options to:
- View the recurring template
- Confirm the transaction early
- Skip this occurrence

**Confirmation-Required Transactions:**
For scheduled transactions requiring your approval, tapping opens a confirmation dialog with options to:
- Confirm the transaction
- Skip this occurrence
- Edit before confirming

**Transfers:**
Opens the Edit Transfer screen to modify transfer details.

**Balance Adjustments:**
Opens the Edit Balance screen to modify the adjustment.

Long-press a transaction (except previews and confirmation-required ones) for edit, duplicate, and delete. If it belongs to a receipt, **Edit receipt** opens that receipt with all of its items.

---

## Adding New Transactions

The floating action button(s) at the bottom of the screen let you quickly add new entries. The available options depend on the context you're viewing:

### Global View (All Transactions)

A single **Add Transaction** button opens the Add Transaction screen with the selected date pre-filled. To create a receipt from there, use expense mode and tap the split icon next to the **Category** field.

### Account View

A single + button opens a menu with options to:
- **Add Transaction** - Record a new expense or income for this account (available for foreign-currency accounts as well as main-currency accounts)
- **Add Receipt** - Add or enter a receipt for this account (only for accounts in your main currency; hidden for foreign-currency accounts)
- **Transfer Between Accounts** - Create a transfer involving this account
- **Balance Increase** - Add a positive balance adjustment
- **Balance Decrease** - Add a negative balance adjustment

### Category View

A single + button opens the Add Transaction screen with:
- The selected category pre-filled
- The selected date pre-filled

---

## Context Awareness

The Day Transactions Screen adapts based on where you access it from:

### From the Main Transactions Screen
- Shows all transactions across all accounts and categories
- Both floating action buttons (receipt and add) are available

### From an Account
- Shows only transactions for that specific account
- Account-specific add options are available
- Account badges may be hidden since you're already viewing one account

### From a Category
- Shows only transactions for that specific category
- Add transaction opens with the category pre-selected

### From a Contact, Tag, or Section
- Shows only transactions related to that entity
- No floating action button is shown; you cannot add transactions from this screen when viewing by contact, tag, or section

---

## Visual Indicators

### Day Tile Colors

In the calendar grid:
- **Income color** - Income totals for that day (typically green; follows budget section color)
- **Red amounts** - Expense totals for that day
- **Highlighted border** - Currently selected day or today
- **Faded appearance** - Future dates

### Transaction Colors

In the transaction list:
- **Income color with +** - Income transactions (typically green; follows budget section)
- **Section color** - Expense transactions (matches budget section)
- **Faded appearance** - Preview/scheduled transactions not yet confirmed

---

## Tips for Using the Day Transactions Screen

1. **Quick date navigation** - Use the left/right arrows to quickly check adjacent days
2. **Use the calendar for jumping** - Tap the date in the header to return to the calendar, then choose any day, especially when looking at historical data
3. **Check daily patterns** - The calendar's income/expense indicators help you spot spending patterns at a glance
4. **Selection mode for subtotals** - Use selection mode to quickly calculate the total for specific purchases or categories
5. **Future planning** - View future dates to see upcoming scheduled and recurring transactions
6. **Add transactions on the right date** - When viewing a specific date, new transactions automatically use that date
7. **Month picker for long jumps** - Tap the month name to quickly jump to months far in the past

---

## Navigating Back

Tap the X (close) button in the top-left corner to exit the Day Transactions Screen and return to the previous screen.

---

# Transactions for an account, category, contact, or tag

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/entity-transactions

The Entity Transactions Screen shows all transactions related to a specific item—whether that's an account, budget category, budget section, contact, or tag. This screen provides a focused view of your financial activity filtered to one particular area, helping you understand your spending patterns and track transactions for specific purposes.

## Accessing the Entity Transactions Screen

You can access this screen by tapping on:
- **An account** from the Accounts Screen
- **A budget category** from the Budget Screen
- **A budget section** from the Budget Screen
- **A contact** from the Contacts list
- **A tag** from the Tags list

---

## Screen Layout

### Title Bar

The title bar displays:
- **Back button** (left) - Returns to the previous screen
- **Entity name** - The name of the account, category, section, contact, or tag you're viewing
- **Analytics icon** (pie chart) - Opens [Analytics & Reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics) starting with this entity. Further drill-down selections retain the original entity filter; the Transactions option inside analytics shows the resulting intersection.
- **Search icon** - Opens transaction search filtered to this entity

### Period Picker

Below the title bar, you'll find the period picker that lets you select the date range for viewing transactions.

**Actions:**
- **Tap the period** to open the period selection options where you can choose:
  - This month
  - Last month
  - This year
  - Last year
  - All time
  - Custom date range
- **Calendar icon** (left side) - Opens the Day Transactions view where you can browse transactions on a calendar, day by day

The period picker may also show balance information when viewing an account.

---

## Summary Card

The Summary Card at the top shows financial totals for the selected period.

### For Accounts

When viewing an account, the summary shows:
- **Inflow** - Total money coming into this account (deposits, transfers in)
- **Outflow** - Total money leaving this account (withdrawals, transfers out)

You can expand the summary to see detailed breakdowns. The expanded view shows (in order):
- **Regular income** and **regular expenses** (first row)
- **Transfers received** and **transfers sent** (second row)
- **Balance increases** and **balance decreases** (third row)
- **Opening balance** and **closing balance** for the period (at the bottom)

### For Categories, Sections, Contacts, and Tags

The summary shows:
- **Income** - Total income transactions for this entity
- **Expenses** - Total expense transactions for this entity

### Expense Type Breakdown

For sections, contacts, and tags, you can toggle to see expenses broken down by category type:
- **Needs** - Essential expenses
- **Wants** - Non-essential/discretionary expenses
- **Savings** - Savings contributions

Tap the card to toggle between the standard view and the expense type breakdown.

---

## History and Upcoming Tabs

When you have both past transactions and future scheduled transactions for the entity, the screen displays two toggle buttons:

### History Tab
Shows all transactions from today and earlier, sorted with the most recent transactions first.

### Upcoming Tab
Shows all future transactions (scheduled, recurring, or planned), sorted with the soonest transactions first.

**Tab Information:**
- Each tab displays the total income and expenses for that section
- Income is shown in the income color (from your Income budget section) with a "+" prefix
- Expenses are shown in red with a "-" prefix
- Tap a tab to switch between History and Upcoming views

**Note:** If you only have past transactions or only have future transactions, the tabs won't appear—the screen will automatically show whichever section has data.

---

## Transaction List

Transactions are grouped by date with clear date headers. Each date section shows all transactions that occurred on that day. On account and set views, transactions from the same receipt or the same contact on that day may be grouped together.
