Category, section, contact, tag, category-type, and contact-type views list each receipt item on its own.

### Transaction Display

Each transaction shows information relevant to the entity you're viewing:

- **Category icon** (when not viewing a category/section) - The icon of the budget section
- **Category name** - The budget category this transaction belongs to
- **Amount** - The transaction amount with color coding:
  - Income color (from your Income budget section) with "+" prefix = Income
  - Section color = Expenses

### What's Hidden

Depending on what entity you're viewing, some information is hidden since it would be redundant:
- **Viewing an account** - The account badge is hidden (you already know the account)
- **Viewing a category** - The category name and icon are hidden
- **Viewing a section** - The section icon is hidden
- **Viewing a contact** - The contact badge is hidden
- **Viewing a tag** - The current tag is hidden (other tags still appear)

### Additional Details

Transactions may also display:
- **Receipt icon** - Shown after the row title when the transaction belongs to a receipt. The title is the category name, or the description when you are viewing a category and the transaction has a description. Category, section, contact, tag, category-type, and contact-type lists do not group receipt items, so this icon is how you can tell a line is part of a receipt.
- **Recurring icon (↻)** - Indicates a recurring transaction
- **Question mark icon (?)** - Indicates confirmation is required
- **Swap icon (↔)** - Indicates a transfer between accounts
- **Contact badge** - Shows the associated contact (when not viewing a contact)
- **Account badge** - Shows the account used (when not viewing an account)
- **Description** - Any notes on the transaction
- **Tags** - Hashtags for additional categorization

### Running balance (account views)

When viewing an **account**, each row can show a muted **running balance** directly under the transaction amount. That value is the account balance after that row in the ledger (history walks from the period-end balance backward; upcoming/forecast walks forward from today’s posted balance). Running balance appears only on account entity lists, not on category, section, contact, or tag views.

### Preview Transactions

Future transactions from recurring templates appear slightly faded to indicate they are previews of upcoming scheduled transactions. This also applies to Sets: only occurrences matching the set's include/exclude conditions and amount limits appear, and Upcoming totals include them. When opened from the Sets block on Budget, the initial dates come from the selected budget period. Budget's Include future transactions setting affects Budget amounts only; this screen still shows matching saved transactions and recurring previews using its usual History and Upcoming views.

---

## Transaction Types

### Regular Transactions
Standard income or expense transactions linked to a budget category.

### Transfers (Account View Only)
When viewing an account, you'll see transfers involving that account:
- A swap icon (↔) indicating a transfer
- The other account involved in the transfer
- The transfer amount

### Balance Adjustments (Account View Only)
Manual adjustments to the account balance:
- "Balance Increase" or "Balance Decrease" as the title
- The adjustment amount

---

## Transaction Actions

### Tap a Transaction

**For regular transactions:** Opens the Edit Transaction screen where you can modify all details.

**For preview/recurring transactions:** Opens options to:
- Confirm the transaction
- Skip this occurrence
- Modify the amount or details

**For confirmation-required transactions:** Opens a confirmation dialog with options to confirm, skip, or edit.

**For transfers:** Opens the Edit Transfer screen.

**For balance adjustments:** Opens the Edit Balance screen.

### Long-Press a Transaction

Long-pressing a transaction (except preview and confirmation-required ones) opens the same quick actions as on Transactions: edit, duplicate, delete, and transform to receipt when that expense can become a receipt. If the transaction already belongs to a receipt, **Edit receipt** opens that receipt with all of its items, including items that are not in this category, section, contact, or tag.

---

## Adding New Transactions

### For Account Views

A floating action button (+) appears at the bottom center. Tapping it opens a menu with options:

- **Add Transaction** - Record a new income or expense using this account (available for foreign-currency accounts as well as main-currency accounts)
- **Add Receipt** - Add a receipt and create transactions using this account (only for accounts in your main currency; hidden for foreign-currency accounts)
- **Transfer Between Accounts** - Move money to or from this account
- **Increase Balance** - Add money to this account without creating an income transaction
- **Decrease Balance** - Remove money from this account without creating an expense transaction

### For Category Views

A floating action button (+) appears at the bottom center. Tapping it opens the Add Transaction screen with this category pre-selected.

### For Other Views

Contacts, sections, and tags do not have a floating action button since transactions are created through the main Transactions screen or Budget screen.

---

## Loading More Transactions

The screen initially shows a limited number of transactions for faster loading:
- **History tab** - Shows 100 transactions at a time (for periods longer than 45 days)
- **Upcoming tab** - Shows 90 days of future transactions at a time

### "Show More" Button
When there are additional transactions to display, a "Show More" button appears at the bottom of the list. Tap it to load more transactions.

---

## Empty State

If there are no transactions for the selected entity and period, the screen displays:
- A receipt icon
- A message indicating no transactions exist for this period

---

## Different Views Explained

### Account Transactions View

When you tap an account from the Accounts screen, you see:
- All transactions where this account was used
- Transfers involving this account
- Balance adjustments for this account
- The inflow/outflow summary helps you understand cash flow through this account

**Use this to:** Track spending from a specific card, review bank account activity, or reconcile balances.

### Category Transactions View

When you tap a budget category, you see:
- All transactions assigned to this category
- How much you've spent in this category for the period

**Use this to:** Review all grocery purchases, track entertainment spending, or analyze any specific category.

### Section Transactions View

When you tap a budget section, you see:
- All transactions from all categories within this section
- The combined income or expenses for the entire section

**Use this to:** Get a broader view of spending areas like "Food & Dining" or "Transportation."

### Contact Transactions View

When you tap a contact, you see:
- All transactions associated with this person or business
- Your complete transaction history with this contact

**Use this to:** See how much you've spent at a particular store, track payments to a service provider, or review transactions with a specific person.

### Tag Transactions View

When you tap a tag, you see:
- All transactions that have this tag applied
- Spending patterns for this specific tag

**Use this to:** Track project expenses, vacation spending, or any custom grouping you've created with tags.

---

## Tips for Using This Screen

1. **Use date ranges strategically** - Select "All Time" to see complete history, or narrow to specific months for focused analysis

2. **Check both tabs** - Review History to see what happened and Upcoming to see what's scheduled

3. **Use Analytics** - Tap the pie chart icon for visual charts and deeper insights about this entity

4. **Use Search** - The search function helps you find specific transactions within this entity's history

5. **Expand account summaries** - When viewing accounts, tap the Summary Card to see detailed breakdowns of all transaction types

6. **Review expense types** - For sections, contacts, and tags, toggle the expense breakdown to see needs vs. wants vs. savings

7. **Add transactions directly** - When viewing accounts or categories, use the floating action button to quickly add transactions with that entity pre-selected

---

# Accounts

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/accounts

The Accounts Screen is where you manage all your financial accounts. You can organize your bank accounts, cash, credit cards, investments, and any other accounts you use to manage money. Accounts are organized into groups to help you keep things tidy and see your total balances at a glance.

## Accessing the Accounts Screen

You can access the Accounts Screen by:
- Tapping the "Accounts" tab in the bottom navigation

---

## Understanding Account Groups

Account groups help you organize related accounts together. For example, you might have:
- **Main Accounts** - Your primary checking account, savings, and cash
- **Credit Cards** - All your credit cards in one place
- **Investments** - Brokerage accounts, retirement funds
- **Savings Goals** - Separate accounts for vacation, emergency fund, etc.
- **Debts** - Loans, mortgages, money you owe

Each group displays its own icon and shows the combined total balance of all accounts within it (when all accounts share the same currency).

---

## Screen Layout

### Account Groups

The main area displays your account groups as expandable cards. Each group card shows:

- **Group icon** (on the left) - A visual identifier for the group type
- **Group name** - The name you gave the group (e.g., "Main Accounts", "Savings")
- **Total balance** (on the right) - The combined balance of all accounts in the group
  - Only shown when all accounts in the group use the same currency
  - Positive balances appear in the app's primary color
  - Negative balances appear in red
- **Menu button** (three dots) - Opens group actions

### Expanding and Collapsing Groups

- **Tap the group header** to expand or collapse it
- When expanded, you'll see all accounts within that group
- When a group has no accounts, an **Add account** button appears inside the group card for quick access
- The app remembers which groups you had expanded, so they stay that way when you return

### Individual Accounts

Within each expanded group, accounts are listed showing:

- **Account name** - The name you gave the account (e.g., "Chase Checking", "Cash Wallet")
- **Default indicator** (star icon) - Shows if this is your default account
- **Description** - Any notes you added about the account
- **Balance** - Current account balance with currency symbol
  - Positive balances appear in the primary color
  - Negative balances appear in red
- **Goal progress** - If the account has a goal, the row shows current balance vs target balance, remaining or over-goal amount, remaining percentage, and a progress bar
- **Menu button** (three dots) - Opens account actions

---

## Quick Action Buttons

At the bottom of the screen, you'll find floating action buttons for common tasks:

### When You Have One or More Accounts

- **Decrease Balance** (minus icon) - Quickly record a balance decrease on any account
- **Increase Balance** (plus icon) - Quickly record a balance increase on any account

### When You Have Two or More Accounts

- **Transfer** (swap arrows icon) - Move money between your accounts

These buttons provide fast access to the most common account operations without needing to open the menu.

---

## Top Bar Actions

When at least one active account exists, the top bar shows:

- **Match bank statement** (upload icon) - Opens Statement Import. Free users see a gold **Pro** badge on the icon; tapping it opens the Pro upgrade page instead of import. Pro users go straight to Statement Import (choose the account there if it is not already selected) → [Bank statement matching](https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching)
- **More menu** (menu icon) - Opens the options listed below

## Top Bar Menu

Tap the menu icon in the top right corner to access additional options:

### Add Group
Create a new account group to organize your accounts. Groups can have custom names and icons.

### Add Account
Create a new account. You'll need to:
- Select which group it belongs to
- Enter a name for the account
- Set the starting balance
- Choose the currency
- Optionally add a description
- Optionally set it as your default account
- Optionally set a balance goal for the account

### Transfer Between Accounts
Move money from one account to another. This is useful for:
- Recording bank transfers
- Moving money between checking and savings
- Tracking credit card payments
- Recording any money movement between your accounts

### Increase Balance
Add money to an account without creating a regular income transaction. Use this for:
- Corrections when your balance doesn't match your bank
- Initial deposits when setting up a new account
- Any balance adjustment that shouldn't appear as regular income

### Decrease Balance
Remove money from an account without creating a regular expense transaction. Use this for:
- Corrections when your balance doesn't match your bank
- Fees or charges that don't fit a budget category
- Any balance adjustment that shouldn't appear as regular expenses

### Match bank statement
Import a CSV or XLSX bank statement and reconcile rows with existing transactions (same destination as the top-bar upload icon). Free users see a **Pro** badge on this row and are sent to the Pro upgrade page; Pro users open Statement Import → [Bank statement matching](https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching)

### Change Order
Rearrange the order of your account groups and accounts within groups. Drag items to reorder them however you prefer.

### Archive
View and manage your archived accounts and groups. Archiving lets you hide accounts you no longer use while keeping their history.

---

## Account Actions

### Tapping an Account

Tap any account to view all transactions for that account. This opens a filtered transaction list showing:
- All income and expenses involving this account
- Transfers to and from this account
- Balance adjustments
- The account's transaction history over time

### Long-Pressing an Account (or Tapping the Menu Button)

Opens a menu with these options:

- **Increase Balance** - Add money to this specific account
- **Decrease Balance** - Remove money from this specific account
- **Match bank statement** - Import a CSV or XLSX bank statement for this account and reconcile statement rows with existing transactions (Pro; free users see a **Pro** badge and are sent to upgrade) → [Bank statement matching](https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching)
- **Flow Chart** - Open an account-specific flow screen with inflow, outflow, and balance trends for that account across the selected period
- **Analytics** - Open the general Analytics screen filtered to this account for breakdowns by category, contact, tag, description, and more
- **Edit** - Change the account's name, description, currency, balance, group, default status, or goal
- **Archive** - Hide the account from the main list (keeps all history)
- **Delete** - Permanently remove the account (only available if the account has no transactions)

**Note:** You cannot delete an account that has transactions. Archive it instead to hide it while preserving your financial history.

---

## Account Flow Chart

The account flow chart is a dedicated screen for understanding how money moves through one account over time.

### What It Shows

- **Period picker in the top bar** - Change the date range for this account
- **Summary card** - Total inflow and outflow for the selected period
- **Flow type filters** - Switch between All, Inflow, Outflow, and Balance
- **Trend chart** - View the account's movement grouped by days, weeks, months, or years depending on the selected range

Unlike the general Analytics screen, this account flow view is focused on money moving in and out of the selected account itself.

---

## Account Goals

Account goals let you track progress toward a target balance on a specific account. They are useful for savings targets such as an emergency fund or vacation fund, and can also represent a balance you want to reach when paying down an account.

### Setting a Goal

When creating or editing an account, tap **Set goal** to show the goal fields:
- **Target balance** - The balance you want this account to reach
- **Goal start** - The balance where progress starts; this defaults to the account's current balance when you enable the goal

If you set a target balance and leave Goal start empty, Budgetum uses the account balance as the starting point for goal progress.

### How Goals Are Displayed

Accounts with goals show extra progress information directly in the account list:
- Current balance compared with the target balance
- Amount remaining until the target, or the amount over the target after passing it
- Remaining or over-goal percentage
- A small progress bar

Progress is calculated from the Goal start balance to the Target balance. If the target is higher than the start, progress increases as the balance grows. If the target is lower than the start, progress increases as the balance goes down toward the target.

### Editing or Removing a Goal

Open the account menu and choose **Edit** to change goal values. Clearing the target balance removes the goal from the account.

---

## Account Group Actions

Long-press a group header (or tap the menu button) to see group options:

- **Add Account** - Create a new account within this group
- **Edit** - Change the group's name or icon
- **Archive** - Hide the entire group (and all its accounts) from the main list
- **Delete** - Permanently remove the group (only available if the group has no accounts)

---

## Creating a New Account

When adding a new account, you'll fill in:

### Required Fields
- **Group** - Which group this account belongs to
- **Name** - A unique name for the account (e.g., "Main Checking", "Vacation Savings"). Duplicate names are not allowed.
- **Starting Balance** - The current balance in this account

### Optional Fields
- **Currency** - Defaults to your app's primary currency, but can be different for foreign accounts. Foreign-currency accounts can be used for normal income and expense transactions (with a separate budget amount), for multi-currency transfers, and for balance tracking. Receipts and the default-account option stay limited to the primary currency.
- **Description** - Notes about the account (e.g., "Emergency fund - don't touch!")
- **Set as Default** - Make this your default account for new transactions (only available for accounts using your primary currency)
- **Goal** - Optional target balance and starting balance used to show progress in the account list

---

## Transfers Between Accounts

When transferring money, you'll specify:

- **From Account** - The account sending money
- **To Account** - The account receiving money
- **From Amount** - How much is leaving the source account
- **To Amount** - How much is arriving in the destination account (automatically matches the from amount, but you can change it for currency conversions or fee adjustments)
- **Date** - When the transfer happened
- **Description** - Optional notes about the transfer
- **Make Recurring** - Set up automatic repeating transfers

**Multi-Currency Transfers:** If you're transferring between accounts with different currencies, you can enter different amounts for "from" and "to" to account for exchange rates. The amount picker may offer an optional market-rate quick suggestion between the two currencies. When both amounts are filled, the form can also show a muted **implied rate** helper under the amount fields (destination ÷ source from the numbers you entered)—this is not a live market quote.

**Scheduled Transfers:** If you set a future date, you can optionally mark the transfer as requiring confirmation before it affects your balances.

---

## Balance Adjustments

Balance adjustments let you correct your account balance without creating regular transactions. This is useful when:

- Your tracked balance doesn't match your actual bank balance
- You find discrepancies during reconciliation
- You need to account for fees that don't fit a category
- You receive or lose money outside your normal transactions

### Increase Balance
Adds money to an account. Records when and why the balance increased.

### Decrease Balance
Removes money from an account. Records when and why the balance decreased.

Both adjustment types support:
- Setting a specific date
- Adding a description
- Making it recurring (for regular adjustments like monthly bank fees)
- Requiring confirmation for future-dated adjustments

---

## Archive

The Archive stores accounts and groups you've hidden from your main view. Archiving is perfect for:
- Old bank accounts you've closed
- Credit cards you've paid off
- Temporary accounts you no longer use
- Keeping your main list clean and focused

### Viewing the Archive

Access the archive from the top bar menu. Here you'll see all archived groups and accounts.

### Archive Actions

For **archived groups**:
- **Restore** - Bring the group back to your main list
- **Delete** - Permanently remove (only if the group has no accounts)

For **archived accounts**:
- **View Transactions** - See the account's transaction history
- **Restore** - Bring the account back to its group
- **Delete** - Permanently remove (only if the account has no transactions)

---

## Reordering Accounts and Groups

From "Change Order" in the menu, you can customize how your accounts appear:

### Reordering Groups
Drag and drop groups to arrange them in your preferred order. The first group appears at the top of your Accounts screen.

### Reordering Accounts Within a Group
Tap a group to open the account order view for that group, then drag and drop to reorder its accounts. This affects the display order within that group.

---

## Getting Started Help

When you first open the Accounts screen (or have no account groups), you'll see a helpful guide explaining:

1. How account groups work
2. Suggested group structures
3. Examples of common setups

You can dismiss this guide once you're comfortable with the concept. The guide provides examples like:
- **Main Accounts** - Checking, Savings, Cash
- **Debts** - Credit Cards, Loans, Mortgages
- **Investments** - Stocks, Retirement, Crypto
- **Savings Goals** - Emergency Fund, Vacation, Car
- **Other** - Gift Cards, Prepaid Cards

---

## Tips for Using Accounts

1. **Use groups strategically** - Organize accounts by purpose (spending, saving, debt) rather than by institution

2. **Set a default account** - Your most-used account should be the default, so it's pre-selected when adding transactions

3. **Keep balances accurate** - Regularly compare your app balances to your actual accounts and use balance adjustments to fix any differences

4. **Use descriptions** - Add notes to accounts to remember their purpose or any special rules

5. **Use transfers for internal movement** - When you move money between your own accounts, use Transfer rather than creating separate income/expense transactions

6. **Consider negative balances** - Credit cards and loans typically have negative balances, which is normal and expected

---

# Bank statement matching

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/bank-statement-matching

The Statement Import screen helps you reconcile one account in Budgetum with a bank statement file. You import a CSV or XLSX file, tell Budgetum which columns contain the date, amount, and description, and then compare the imported statement rows with transactions that already exist in that account.

This feature is designed to speed up account reconciliation. It does not replace your full transaction history automatically. Instead, it helps you match, create, or ignore rows one by one or in batches.

## Accessing Statement Import

You can open Statement Import from the **Accounts** screen in several ways:
- **Top-bar upload icon** (**Match bank statement**) — opens Statement Import; pick the account on the import screen if needed
- **Accounts More menu** — same **Match bank statement** action
- **Account row more menu** (or long-press the account row) — **Match bank statement** for that account (account is pre-selected)

Free users see a gold **Pro** badge on these entry points and are sent to the Pro upgrade page instead of import.

**Availability:**
- Available only in **Budgetum Pro**
- Each import belongs to a single account
- The English action label is **Match bank statement** (no Beta suffix on that action string)

---

## What Statement Import Does

Statement Import compares:
- **Imported statement rows** from your bank file
- **Existing account transactions** already recorded in Budgetum

It helps you identify:
- Rows that already match existing transactions
- Existing transactions that appear in Budgetum but were not matched to the imported statement
- Statement rows that still need action

This works for:
- Regular income and expense transactions
- Transfers
- Balance increases and decreases
- Receipt groups, when several receipt items together equal one statement amount

---

## Help Card

Before or while setting up an import (account + file + column mapping), a dismissible help card can appear with short steps and matching tips (auto-matched rows, unmatched `?` rows, and that starting a new import only clears statement rows for that account).

- Title: **Match your bank statement**
- Dismiss with **Got it!**
- Dismissal is remembered; **More → Tips & Assistance → Reset Tutorial** restores it along with other tutorial hints

---

## Supported Files

You can import:
- **CSV**
- **XLSX**

For best results:
- The file should contain a clear **header row**
- The header row should be placed directly above the transaction data
- The data should include at least a date, a description, and an amount representation

If Budgetum cannot detect the header row automatically, you can often fix it with **Import options** (the **more** menu on the **Match columns** card) instead of choosing another file:

- **Select header row** — pick which row in the file contains column titles (Date, Amount, Description, etc.). Budgetum re-reads the grid from that row.
- **Date format** — choose how ambiguous numeric dates (for example `03/04/2026`) should be interpreted: automatic from your device locale, day/month/year, month/day/year, or year/month/day.

If the file cannot be read at all, choose a different file or export format.

---

## Import Setup

Before saving the import, you configure how the source file maps into Budgetum.

### 1. Select a file

Tap the **Statement file** field and choose a CSV or XLSX file from your device.

While Budgetum processes the file, it shows status messages such as:
- Reading the selected file
- Analyzing the file structure
- Auto-matching columns
- Validating rows

### 2. Match columns

Use the **more** menu (three dots) on the **Match columns** card when you need **Select header row** or **Date format** (optional).

After the file is read, Budgetum asks you to match source columns to required fields:
- **Date column**
- **Description column**
- **Amount column**, or separate **Credit** and **Debit** columns

Each required field must use a different source column.

### 3. Choose an amount mode

You can import statement amounts in three ways:

### Signed amount (+/-)
- Use this when one amount column already includes positive and negative values
- Positive values are treated as money entering the account
- Negative values are treated as money leaving the account

### Not signed (expense by default)
- Use this when the statement has a single amount column without signs
- Imported rows are treated as expenses by default

### Credit and debit columns
- Use this when the bank exports money in and money out into separate columns
- Budgetum calculates one signed amount from those two fields

### 4. Review the preview

Budgetum shows a preview of the first imported rows using the selected columns so you can confirm the mapping before saving.

### 5. Save the import

When validation succeeds, tap the **check** button in the top bar.

Saving the import:
- Stores the parsed rows for that account
- Remembers your column names for future auto-matching
- Starts the reconciliation view
- Builds matching rules from exact matches for future suggestions

---

## Validation Rules

Budgetum checks the file before it saves anything.

Common validation requirements:
- The file must contain rows
- The required mapped columns must exist
- The date and description must be matched
- The amount mapping must match the selected amount mode
- Required fields must use different columns
- Each row must contain a valid date
- Each row must contain a valid amount

If any row fails validation, Budgetum shows the row number and stops the save so you can correct the mapping or choose another file.

---

## Reconciliation View

After saving, the screen changes from setup mode to a date-grouped reconciliation list.

Rows are grouped by date and may appear in three states:

### Matched rows

These statement rows were matched to one or more existing transactions in the selected account.

**How automatic matching works:**
- Budgetum builds match **candidates** from the account’s transactions in the imported date range:
  - Each normal transaction is one candidate (amount is the signed movement for this account)
  - Receipt lines that share a receipt ID are combined into one **receipt-group** candidate whose amount is the sum of those lines
- A statement row auto-matches only when there is exactly **one** remaining candidate with the **same date** and the **same signed amount** (compared to the cent)
- If several transactions share the same date and amount, Budgetum does **not** guess. The row stays unmatched until you choose manually
- Each candidate can be used by only one statement row

Receipt groups can therefore match a single bank charge that equals the total of several receipt items.

Matched entries appear slightly faded to show they are already reconciled. Opening a matched transaction can offer **Unlink from statement** to clear that link.

### Existing-only rows

These are transactions that already exist in Budgetum for that account and date range but were not paired with any imported row.

This helps you notice:
- Transactions entered in Budgetum but not present in the statement
- Duplicate or extra records
- Timing differences between your app and the bank

### Unmatched rows

These are statement rows that still need your decision.

Unmatched rows may show suggestion badges for:
- **Category**
- **Contact**
- **Transfer to/from an account**

Those suggestions come from learned matching rules based on previous exact matches (see below). The badges may highlight the most-used pattern. When approving a row with multiple compatible category/contact or transfer variants, you always choose a variant before anything is created.

---

## Row Actions

Tap an unmatched row to open actions.

### Approve

**Approve** creates one transaction using the statement date and amount, the current account, and a learned category/contact or transfer variant. A transfer variant shows **Transfer to {account}** for outgoing amounts or **Transfer from {account}** for incoming amounts. It creates a transfer between the current account and the remembered account, using the statement amount for both sides and leaving the transfer description empty. Both accounts must be active and use the same currency.

Approve is disabled if no compatible category or transfer suggestion exists; use **Create transaction** or **Transfer** to choose fields yourself. Different-currency transfers still use the **Transfer** form so you can enter both amounts.

With one compatible variant, creation starts immediately. With multiple variants, **Select variant** opens first. Variants are sorted by usage, most-used first; ties use the most recent usage. No counts are shown beside variants. Selecting one creates the transaction; dismissing the picker creates nothing.

### Approve all (N)

In an unmatched row's actions, **Approve all (N)** appears when more than one unmatched row in the same account's current import shares the same cleaned description and can use at least one of the selected row's compatible variants. The group includes rows hidden by search and spans all dates in the import. Each transaction keeps its own date and amount.

The variant choice works like **Approve**, and the selected category/contact or transfer account applies to compatible rows in the group:
- An expense category accepts outgoing expenses and incoming refunds.
- An income category accepts incoming amounts only. Outgoing rows stay unmatched.
- A transfer variant accepts only its remembered direction: outgoing to that account or incoming from it. Rows in the opposite direction stay unmatched.
- Zero amounts are not approved.

**N** is the eligible group size before choosing a variant. The number created can be smaller when the chosen variant excludes rows with an incompatible direction. A completion message reports how many transactions were created. Already matched rows are excluded, and further approval actions are unavailable while approval is in progress. Transfer approval checks current matches again, so a transfer already created from the other account’s statement can match instead of being created twice. Matching still requires the same date and account amount. If several existing transfers could fit, use **Select existing** to resolve the ambiguity; approval leaves those rows unmatched.

### Create transaction

Creates a normal income or expense transaction from the statement row.

Budgetum pre-fills:
- The selected account
- The statement date
- The absolute amount
- Suggested category and contact, if available

### Transfer

Creates a transfer between accounts using the statement row.

Budgetum pre-fills:
- The statement date
- The amount
- The selected account as the source or destination, depending on whether the row is outgoing or incoming

### Increase balance

Creates a balance increase linked to the imported row.

### Decrease balance

Creates a balance decrease linked to the imported row.

### Select existing

Opens **Select transactions** so you can manually link the statement row to existing Budgetum activity on the **same date**.

You can select:
- One transaction whose amount already equals the statement amount, or
- Several same-day candidates (including receipt groups) whose amounts **add up exactly** to the statement amount

The screen shows:
- **Remaining** amount still needed
- **Selected of target** totals
- A check action that stays disabled until the selected total matches the statement amount exactly

This is useful when:
- More than one possible transaction exists for the same date and amount (auto-match stayed unmatched on purpose)
- One bank charge covers several Budgetum transactions
- You already recorded the activity and just want to confirm the link

Manual links are remembered by a row fingerprint (account, date, amount, cleaned description) and the selected transaction IDs. If you clear the import and re-import the same statement later, Budgetum can restore those links automatically when the matching transactions are still available.

### Ignore

Removes the imported row from the saved import without deleting any real transaction.

Use this when the statement row should not be tracked in Budgetum.

---

## Bulk Actions And Learned Suggestions

Statement Import can learn from successful exact matches.

When Budgetum finds a reliable exact match, it can remember:
- A cleaned version of the statement description (noisy prefixes, dates, times, and short reference codes are reduced so similar merchant text still matches)
- The category used
- The contact used
- For a transfer, the other account and direction, stored separately for incoming and outgoing rows
- How often that pattern was used

Transfer patterns are learned both when you create a transfer using a statement row’s **Transfer** action and when that row is matched to one existing transfer, automatically or through **Select existing**. The date and amount must match the row. Only transfers between accounts with the same currency and equal amounts on both sides teach quick-approval patterns; a grouped match to several transactions does not. Transfer suggestions are hidden if either account is archived, the other account is deleted, or the accounts no longer use the same currency.

Learning is specific to the imported account and statement description. Incoming and outgoing transfer patterns remain separate even when their descriptions are identical; the amount’s sign determines direction, without removing “from” or “to” from the description.

Later, unmatched rows with a similar cleaned description can show suggested badges. Use **Approve** for one row or **Approve all (N)** in that row's actions for repeated descriptions. When multiple compatible patterns exist, choose one in **Select variant**, ordered by usage and then recency. There is no global action to create transactions across unrelated descriptions.

---

## Search And Visibility Options

After an import is saved, the top bar offers extra tools:

### Search

Search helps filter the reconciliation list by terms such as:
- Description text
- Date
- Amount
- Suggested category
- Suggested contact
- Suggested transfer account and direction

### Show or hide matched rows

You can hide already matched transactions to focus only on what still needs attention. Use the eye icon in the top bar (**Hide matched transactions** / **Show matched transactions**).

When matched rows are hidden and nothing else is left (no unmatched statement rows and no existing-only transactions), the screen shows a check mark with **All rows are matched**: the account is fully reconciled for this import. Tap the eye icon again to see the matched rows.

---

## Start New Import

From the **more** menu, you can choose **Start new import**.

This action:
- Clears the saved imported statement rows for that account
- Keeps your real Budgetum transactions
- Keeps learned column matches
- Lets you import a fresh file for the same account

Use this when you selected the wrong file, need a newer statement, or want to restart reconciliation from scratch.

---

## Important Notes

- Statement Import is **account-specific**
- Matching compares statement rows only against transactions in that account and within the imported date range
- Auto-match requires a **unique** same-date, same-amount candidate; duplicates stay unmatched until you use **Select existing**
- You can match one statement row to **multiple** same-day transactions when their amounts sum to the statement amount
- Manual matches can persist across clearing and re-importing the same statement file for that account
- Budgetum does not delete existing transactions when you restart or clear an import
- Ignoring a row removes only the imported statement row, not any transaction
- Manual or auto-linked rows can later be opened in their normal edit screens, where you can unlink them from the statement

---

## Tips For Best Results

1. Use statement files with a clear header row directly above the data.
2. Start with accounts you reconcile often, such as your main checking account or card.
3. If possible, import a larger date range instead of a very short statement. More rows give Budgetum more chances to auto-match existing transactions and learn useful category/contact suggestions.
4. If your file uses separate money-in and money-out columns, choose **Credit and debit columns**.
5. Hide matched rows after the first pass to focus on what still needs action.
6. When several Budgetum transactions share one bank charge, use **Select existing** and multi-select until Remaining reaches zero.
7. If same-day duplicates block auto-match, that is intentional—use **Select existing** to pick the correct one.
8. Let the feature learn over time. Repeated exact matches improve future suggestions for categories and contacts.
9. When **Select variant** opens after Approve or Approve all, pick the category/contact or transfer pattern that fits the statement description. Incoming refunds can use an expense category.

---

# Analytics and reports

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/analytics

The Analytics screen provides visual charts and detailed breakdowns of your spending and income patterns. It helps you understand where your money goes, identify trends over time, and make informed financial decisions.

## Accessing Analytics

You can open Analytics from:
- The Analytics action on the Budget screen
- The "Analytics" option in a category's menu on the Budget screen
- The "Analytics" option in a section's menu on the Budget screen
- The pie chart icon when viewing an account, contact, or tag's transactions
- The **Analytics** action in a saved set’s menu

For accounts, there is also a separate **Flow Chart** screen available from the account menu on the Accounts screen. That view is different from Analytics: it focuses on account inflow, outflow, and balance trends for one account rather than category/contact/tag-style breakdowns.

Analytics can be viewed for:
- Your entire budget (all transactions)
- A specific account
- A specific budget section
- A specific category
- A specific contact
- A specific tag
- A specific expense type (Needs, Wants, or Savings)
- A contact type (such as Stores)
- A saved set, including its include/exclude conditions

---

## Screen Layout

### Title Bar

The top bar shows:

- **Back button** - Return to the previous screen
- **Title** - The current entity (e.g., "Groceries" or "Store A").
- **View toggle** - Switch between Breakdown view (pie chart icon) and Trends view (bar chart icon)
- **More analytics (⋮)** - Opens extra analytics views. Currently includes **Spending calendar** (full-year daily spending heatmap)

### Breadcrumbs

After drilling down, a compact, horizontally scrollable text path appears **below the summary** in both Breakdown and Trends, for example `Vacation › Groceries › Store A`. The app-bar title still shows the current entity. Tap an earlier breadcrumb to return to that screen with its period and selected view restored; Back returns one level. When the selection has no data, the path remains available above the empty state.

### Period Picker

Below the title bar, the period picker lets you select the date range for analysis:

- **Compare icon** (⇄, left side of the period picker) - Opens **Compare period** options so you can compare the current range with a previous period or the same period last year (see [Period comparison](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics#period-comparison) below). The icon is brighter when comparison is active.
- **Left/Right arrows** - Navigate between periods (month, year, etc.)
- **Start date** - Tap to open the date picker and set a custom start date; the date picker offers quick options such as "This month" and "This year" (select full month or full year).
- **End date** - Tap to open the date picker and set a custom end date
- **Dropdown** (down arrow) - Opens a list of quick period options: This month, This quarter, This half-year, This year, Previous year, All time

---

## Period comparison

Period comparison lets you judge whether income and spending are up or down versus another date range. It applies to the **summary card**, **breakdown list**, and **trends** details while comparison is enabled.

### How to enable it

1. Tap the **compare arrows** icon on the left of the period picker
2. Choose one option in the bottom sheet:
   - **Previous period** - The equally long range immediately before your current start–end dates. For whole-month selections (for example one month, one quarter, or a half-year of full months), Budgetum shifts by that many calendar months. For other custom ranges, it shifts by the same number of days.
   - **Same period last year** - The same start and end dates shifted back one year (day is clamped to the last valid day of the month when needed, for example Feb 29 → Feb 28)
3. To turn it off, open the sheet again and tap **Disable comparison**

The sheet shows the resolved comparison date range under each option so you can confirm what will be used.

### What changes when comparison is on

- **Summary card** - Income and expense totals show change indicators versus the compared period
- **Breakdown list** - Each row can show amount and percentage change versus the same item in the compared period (higher spending is treated as worse for expenses; higher income is better for income)
- **Trends** - Selected-period details can include comparison deltas when comparison data is available

Period comparison is separate from the Trends **vs Income** overlay (which compares expenses to income inside the same selected period).

---

## Summary Card

At the top of the content area, a Summary Card shows:

- **Income** - Total money received in the period
- **Expenses** - Total money spent in the period
- **Remaining** - The difference (income minus expenses); shown in Trends view only when you have income, and not shown in Breakdown view

When period comparison is enabled, income and expense lines also show how they changed versus the compared period.

The summary covers the full selected period and every active filter, regardless of how many transaction rows are currently displayed. It shows gross expenses and received income, including refunds (offset income). For a $100 purchase and a $20 refund, the summary shows $100 expenses and $20 income; the expense breakdown shows $80 net spending. See [Refunds and tag allocation](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics#refunds-and-tag-allocation).

---

## Breakdown View (Pie Chart)

The Breakdown view shows how your spending or income is distributed across different categories, contacts, or other groupings.

### Income/Expense Dropdown

When you have both income and expenses, a dropdown (top right in the filter area) lets you switch between:
- **Expenses** - See how your spending is distributed
- **Income** - See how your income is distributed

### Breakdown Type

Below the income/expense dropdown, filter buttons let you choose what to break down by. Available breakdowns depend on what you're viewing:

| Starting context | Possible breakdowns |
|---|---|
| Budget (all) | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts |
| Account | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Descriptions |
| Section | Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Category | Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Contact | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Contact type | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Tag | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Expense type | Sections, Categories, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |
| Saved set | Sections, Categories, Expense Types, Contacts, Contact Types, Tags, Accounts, Descriptions |

Only breakdowns that separate the current transactions into at least two different nonempty groups appear. Single-group breakdowns and tags attached to exactly the same purchases are omitted. A grouping already selected in the navigation path is not offered again.

Equal amounts do not make a grouping redundant: two stores with $50 each still represent different purchases. Groups may overlap. If both tags occur on every matching transaction, Tags adds no split and is hidden. A single populated group plus transactions without that value is also hidden; no extra “Unassigned” group is created.

### Transactions option

**Transactions** is the last option in the existing, left-aligned selector. It uses the standard dense transaction rows, grouped by date and then by receipt/contact where possible. Expenses includes matching refunds; Income excludes refunds. Tap a group to inspect its matching transactions, or use the usual transaction edit and long-press actions.

- The percentage control is hidden while Transactions is selected.
- When no useful breakdown remains, transactions appear automatically and the redundant selector is hidden.
- Initially about 100 transactions are displayed. A receipt/contact group crossing the cutoff is included in full, so a page can exceed 100. **Show more** extends the list by another approximately 100 transactions without splitting groups.
- Groups contain only transactions matching the active analytics filters, even if the original receipt contains other purchases.
- The display limit does not affect totals, percentages, comparisons, or charts.
- Changing periods reevaluates the available breakdowns. An explicitly selected Transactions view stays selected.

### Percentage Mode (Expenses Only)

When viewing an expense breakdown and the period has income, a percentage control lets you choose how percentages are calculated:

- **% of Expenses** - Each item’s share of the positive net expense totals in the breakdown. Rows with zero or negative net spending show 0%.
- **% of Period Income** - Each item as a percentage of your total income for the period
- **% of Entity Income** - Each item as a percentage of income for this specific entity (shown only when viewing an account, contact, tag, etc. that has income and where that entity's income differs from total period income)

This helps you understand spending relative to what you earned.

### Breakdown List

The main area shows a list of items with:

**For each item:**
- **Icon and name** - The category, section, contact, or tag
- **Amount** - Total spent or received. When viewing expenses, if the item has offset income (matched income), a small “+X” shows the offset amount and the main amount is net (expense minus offset).
- **Percentage** - Share of the total
- **Progress bar** - Visual representation of the proportion
- **Period comparison deltas** (when enabled) - Amount and/or percentage change versus the compared period

Items are sorted by net amount (largest first).

**Tapping an item** adds it to the current analytics selection and opens the next level for the same period and income/expense mode. Earlier selections remain active, including saved-set conditions: Vacation → Groceries → Store A shows only grocery purchases at that store within Vacation. Descriptions open matching transactions directly.

Changing dates or comparing periods keeps every selection in your analytics path. For example, changing months while viewing `Vacation › Groceries › Store A` shows that month’s grocery purchases at Store A within Vacation. It does not switch to all Store A purchases. Returning through breadcrumbs restores the earlier screen’s period and selection. Analytics refreshes after transaction changes and after closing a transaction group.

---

## Trends View (Bar Chart)

The Trends view shows how your spending or income changes over time, helping you spot patterns and trends.

### Display Type

Toggle buttons let you choose what to display:

**Available display types:**
- **All Expenses** - Total expenses over time
- **Needs+Wants** - All expenses excluding savings (when you have both savings and other expenses)
- **Needs** - Only essential expense categories (when you have them)
- **Wants** - Only discretionary expense categories (when you have them)
- **Savings** - Only savings categories (when you have them)
- **Income** - Total income over time
- **Remaining** - Balance (income minus expenses) over time (when you have both income and expenses)
- **Saved + remaining** - Running total of savings plus remaining money (when you have income, expenses, and savings)

Only types that have data appear as options.

### Time Period

The chart groups data into time buckets (one bar per day, week, month, or year). You choose the grouping via a period selector; only periods that make sense for your date range are offered:

- **Days** - One bar per day. Available only when the selected range is about 2 months or less (62 days or fewer).
- **Weeks** - One bar per week. Available when the range is about 4 months or less (124 days or fewer).
- **Months** - One bar per month. Available when the range is less than about 3 years.
- **Years** - One bar per year. Always available, regardless of date range.

For example, "This month" will typically offer Days and Weeks; "This year" will offer Weeks, Months, and Years; "All time" might offer only Months and Years. Tap the period selector (showing the current grouping) to switch.

### Income Comparison (vs Income)

When viewing expense data and you have income:
- A toggle appears: **vs Income**
- Enable it to overlay your income on the expense chart
- This helps visualize if you're spending more or less than you earn in the same selected period

This is different from **period comparison** (previous period / same period last year) controlled from the period picker.

### Section colors on expense bars

When the Trends display type is an expense view (All expenses, Needs+Wants, Needs, Wants, or Savings) and section breakdown data is available, a **Sections** toggle (pie-chart outline icon) appears next to **vs Income**.

- Turn it **on** to paint each expense bar as a **stack of section colors** (each section uses that section’s color from your budget)
- Sections are stacked with the largest overall share toward the bottom for a stable order across periods
- Very small section slices (under about 1% of the bar) are omitted from the stack so the chart stays readable
- Dimmed (non-selected) bars keep the same section colors at lower opacity
- Selecting a period can show the matching section breakdown details using those same section colors

Turn the toggle **off** to return to solid expense bars (theme expense/error color, or income color when the display type is Savings).

### Chart Display

The bar chart shows:

**Axes:**
- **X-axis (bottom)** — Time periods (days, weeks, months, or years); only a subset of labels is shown to keep the chart readable.
- **Y-axis (left)** — Amount in your currency.
- **Bars** — Height is the total for that period. The chart has light horizontal grid lines to help read values.

**Bar colors:**
- **Expenses (solid)** — Theme error color (typically red), so they stay clearly distinct from income. When the display type is "Savings", bars use the app's income color instead.
- **Expenses (section colors)** — When the Sections toggle is on, expense bars are multi-colored stacks using each budget section’s color (see above).
- **Income** — App income color (e.g. green), used for income bars and when "vs Income" is on.
- **Remaining (balance)** — Income color for positive balance, expense (error) color for negative.
- **Saved + remaining** — Income color for positive totals, expense (error) color for negative.

**Grid below the chart:**  
A grid of cells appears below the chart, one cell per time period (only periods with data are shown). Each cell shows the period label and the amount(s) for that period. The grid uses up to four columns and extends downward as needed. When period comparison is enabled, cells can also show change indicators.

**Selecting and scrolling:**
- **Tap a bar** — Selects that period; the view scrolls so the corresponding grid cell is brought into view.
- **Tap a grid cell** — Selects that period and scrolls so the chart is visible. Tapping the same bar or cell again clears the selection.
- The selected bar and its grid cell are highlighted (full color and border); other bars and cells are dimmed. Use this to match a bar to its detail in the grid or to focus on one period.
- With **Sections** enabled, the selected period can show a section breakdown list that matches the stacked bar colors. Tapping a section preserves the existing analytics filters, the selected bar’s date range within the current period, and its expense-type restriction (for example, Needs).

---

## Entity-Specific Analytics

Analytics starts with the entity or saved set you opened it for. Every later selection adds a restriction to that starting context; it does not replace it. The following sections describe the entry views. Actual breakdown choices are limited to useful, unused groupings.

### Budget Analytics (All Transactions)
- All transactions across accounts; no entity filter
- Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, tags, or accounts
- Compare income vs. expenses for the whole budget

### Account Analytics
- Only transactions where this account is the source or destination of money (transfers and balance adjustments are not shown)
- See which categories, contacts, and tags are linked to that account’s income and expenses
- Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, tags, or descriptions
- This is different from the account-specific **Flow Chart** screen on the Accounts screen, which focuses on money moving through the account itself

### Section Analytics
- Only transactions in categories that belong to this section (income and expenses)
- Break down by categories, expense types, contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions
- See how the section’s total is distributed and where it comes from or goes to

### Category Analytics
- Only transactions in this category (income and expenses)
- Break down by contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions
- See where you spend or earn for this category and how it changes over time

### Contact Analytics
- Only transactions linked to this contact (store or person)
- Break down by sections, categories, expense types, tags, accounts, or descriptions
- See what you buy or receive there and how it trends over time

### Tag Analytics
- Only transactions that have this tag
- Break down by sections, categories, expense types, contacts, accounts, or descriptions
- Useful for project or trip expense tracking

### Expense Type Analytics (Needs / Wants / Savings)
- Only transactions in categories of this type (Needs, Wants, or Savings)
- Break down by sections, categories, contacts, tags, accounts, or descriptions
- See how much goes to that type and where it goes

### Saved Set Analytics

- Opens with the set’s resolved period and include/exclude conditions.
- Further selections stay inside the set: `Vacation › Groceries › Store A` means all three conditions apply.
- Changing dates reloads the set for the newly selected period; it does not edit the saved set’s definition.
- [Saved Sets](https://budgetum.app/help/saved-sets) explains how to open and configure a set.

---

## Understanding the Data

### What's Included

Analytics uses only **stored transactions** in the selected date range:
- Income and expense transactions (saved in the app)
- Both manual transactions and those created from receipts
- Transfers and balance adjustments are not loaded for analytics, so they never appear in totals or breakdowns

### What's Excluded

Analytics excludes:
- **Preview (forecasted) transactions** — recurring schedule previews for the period are not included; only saved transactions are used
- **Transfers and balance adjustments** — these are filtered out of the data set for analytics

### Refunds and tag allocation

Refunds (offset income) are included in the summary’s received-income amount and shown alongside purchases in the expense Transactions view. They are excluded from the ordinary Income breakdown. In expense breakdowns, refunds reduce each item’s gross expense to its net amount, including negative net amounts when refunds exceed purchases. If only refunds match your selection, you can still review them in Transactions.

When a transaction has multiple tags, its amount is divided equally between those tags. Refunds use the same allocation: a $100 expense and $20 refund, both tagged A and B, contribute $50 expense and $10 refund to each tag, or $40 net each. Drilling into a tag shows the full matching transactions; its transaction total may therefore differ from that tag’s allocated amount in the parent breakdown.

The spending calendar uses gross daily expenses or ordinary income and excludes refunds from its day shading. Its amounts therefore need not match a net expense breakdown.

### Date Range Matters

The data shown depends on your selected date range:
- Choose "All Time" for complete history
- Use the period dropdown or tap the dates for presets (This month, This year, etc.)
- Use custom start/end dates for specific analysis (e.g., vacation or project period)

---

## Empty State

If there's no data for the selected period and view:
- A message indicates no data is available (the message differs for Breakdown vs Trends)
- Try selecting a different period or breakdown type
- Check that you have transactions in the selected date range

---

## Spending calendar (year view)

**Spending calendar** is a full-screen year heatmap of daily spending (or income) for the same entity you opened Analytics for.

### How to open it

1. On the Analytics screen, tap **More analytics (⋮)** in the app bar
2. Choose **Spending calendar** (“Daily spending for the year”)

The calendar opens for the year of the Analytics end date.

### What it shows

- A vertical year calendar with months in a compact two-column layout
- Each day cell is shaded by that day’s total amount (darker = higher)
- Year navigation with left/right controls in the app bar (you can move back freely; forward only up to the current year)
- If both expenses and income exist for the entity/year, an expenses/income dropdown switches which amounts color the calendar
- Empty years show “No transactions for this year”

### Day drill-down

When a day has an amount greater than zero and day navigation is available, **tap the day** to open its transactions. A calendar opened after drilling down retains every analytics filter and opens the matching day in the analytics Transactions view.

---

## Tips for Using Analytics

1. **Start with the big picture** - Use "All Time" to see overall patterns, then narrow down

2. **Compare periods** - Use the period picker’s compare icon for previous period or same period last year, and also try different months/years manually

3. **Use breakdown types** - Try different breakdowns to find insights:
   - Categories show *what* you spend on
   - Contacts show *where* you spend
   - Tags show *why* you spend

4. **Check vs Income on trends** - Overlay income on expense bars to see if you're living within your means in the same period

5. **Use section colors on trends** - Turn on the Sections toggle to see which budget sections drive each bar

6. **Tap to drill down** - Each selection narrows the current data. Choose Transactions at any level, or continue until transactions appear automatically.

7. **Open the spending calendar** - Use More analytics → Spending calendar to spot high-spend days across a full year

8. **Track expense types** - If you categorize expenses as Needs, Wants, and Savings, the trend view helps you balance them

9. **Use entity analytics** - Open analytics from specific accounts, contacts, or tags for focused insights

10. **Watch for spikes** - The trend chart and spending calendar help identify unusual spending days or months

11. **Review monthly** - Regular analytics review helps you stay on track with your budget goals

---

## Common Questions

**Why don't I see certain breakdown types?**
A breakdown must offer at least two different nonempty groups and must not already be selected in the navigation path. Contacts is hidden if all matching purchases have the same contact; Tags is hidden if every tag covers exactly the same purchases. When no useful grouping remains, the app shows transactions.

**Why are the percentages different from what I expected?**
Check your percentage mode. "% of Expenses" uses positive net expense totals in the breakdown; "% of Income" uses the selected income denominator. Refunds and amounts allocated across multiple tags can affect the displayed shares.

**Can I see analytics for a specific date range?**
Yes. Changing the period reloads the matching data while retaining your starting entity or set and every drill-down filter. Period comparisons apply that same selection to the comparison dates.

**How do I compare this month to last month or last year?**
Tap the compare arrows on the left of the period picker, then choose **Previous period** or **Same period last year**. Disable comparison from the same sheet when you are done.

**Why don't I see section colors on the trend chart?**
Section-colored stacked bars appear only on expense trend types when section data exists, and only after you turn on the Sections toggle (pie-chart outline icon) next to **vs Income**.

**Where is the year spending calendar?**
On Analytics, tap **More analytics (⋮)** → **Spending calendar**.

**Why are some transactions missing from analytics?**
Analytics uses only stored (saved) transactions in the selected date range. Preview (forecasted) transactions from recurring schedules are not included. Transfers and balance adjustments are also excluded from the analytics data.

---

## Desktop Analytics (budgetum.app/analytics)

Desktop Analytics is a separate, browser-based reporting experience for computers. It complements the in-app Analytics screen with larger layouts and additional reports.

### How to open it

1. In the app, go to **More → Advanced Features → Import / Export**
2. Export your transactions (optionally enable **Include analytics data** to get a ZIP with `transactions.csv` plus `analytics.json`)
3. On a computer, open [budgetum.app/analytics](https://budgetum.app/analytics)
4. Choose the exported `.csv` or `.zip` file

You can also open **About desktop analytics** from Import / Export for an in-app preview of the desktop reports, privacy notes, and a copyable link.

### Privacy

Desktop Analytics is built for desktop use and is private and offline in the browser: your chosen file is read locally, and your transaction data does not leave your device.

### What you can explore

Desktop reports include:

- **Overview** - Income, expenses, remaining money, spending mix, and cash flow in one dashboard
- **Money flow** - How money moves across accounts and related activity
- **Breakdown** - Group spending or income by section, category, contact, account, tags, and more
- **Trends** - Compare monthly income and expenses with charts and detailed hover insights
- **Spending calendar** - Monthly grids, yearly strips, and weekday patterns
- **Categories / Contacts / Tags** - Entity-focused reports with trends and related activity
- **Sets** - Use Saved Sets from your export (when analytics metadata is included) as filters
- **Recurring** - Recurring income and expenses by month, plus schedule review
- **Capital** - Net worth style view across assets, liabilities, and account groups over time
- **Transactions** - Search and inspect exported transactions

### CSV vs ZIP

- **CSV only** - Works for transaction-based reports from `transactions.csv`
- **ZIP with analytics data** - Adds `analytics.json` so Desktop Analytics can use richer metadata (icons, colors, recurring templates, saved sets, account details, and similar export extras). Entity matching is name-based because exported entity names are treated as unique for this app

For export steps, columns, and import, see the Import / Export section in the Settings documentation.

---

# Saved Sets

Source: https://budgetum.app/help/saved-sets

The Saved Sets screen lets you save reusable groups of transaction conditions. A set can be used to quickly open a filtered transaction list, review analytics for the matching transactions, or apply bulk changes to all matching transactions in one place.

In the app, this feature is labeled **"Sets"**.

## Accessing the Saved Sets Screen

You can access this screen by:
- Going to **More**
- Opening **Advanced Features**
- Tapping **Sets**

**Note:** Sets is a Pro feature.

---

## What a Saved Set Does

A saved set stores:
- An optional date range
- Include conditions that define which transactions should match
- Exclude conditions that remove unwanted transactions from the result

Once saved, the set becomes a reusable filter. Instead of rebuilding the same search again and again, you can open the set and immediately work with the matching transactions.

Common uses include:
- Reviewing all grocery spending from selected accounts
- Finding transactions for specific contacts or tags
- Building a temporary work set for cleanup or re-categorization
- Applying bulk changes to many matching transactions at once

---

## Screen Layout

The main screen shows all of your saved sets as a vertical list of cards.

### Help Card

A dismissible help card can appear at the top (and as the empty-state content when you have no sets yet). It explains building include/exclude conditions, opening matching transactions or analytics, and using mass update, with short example set ideas.

- Dismiss with **Got it!**
- After dismiss, an empty list shows the normal empty-state message instead
- Dismissal is remembered; **More → Tips & Assistance → Reset Tutorial** restores it

### Top Bar

The top bar contains:
- **Sort icon** - Opens the set ordering screen so you can rearrange saved sets
- **Add icon** - Creates a new saved set

### Saved Set Card

Each set card may show:
- **Set name** - The name you gave the set
- **Link icon** - A small link beside the name when the set is included on Budget
- **Amount summary** - A net total, or separate positive/negative badges when both income and expense are present
- **Transaction count** - A small number showing how many matching transactions were found
- **Condition icons** - Small icons summarizing what the set filters by
- **Period** - The saved date range, such as `Jan 1 - Now`
- **More button** - Opens actions for that set

### Condition Icons

The icon row gives you a quick visual summary of the filters inside the set.

- Section and category filters use the related section icons and colors
- Account filters use the account group's icon
- Contact filters use the contact type icon
- Tag filters use a tag icon
- Description filters use a note icon

Excluded conditions are shown with a red outline so you can tell them apart from included ones.

---

## Opening a Saved Set

### Tap a Set

Tapping a saved set opens a filtered transactions screen for the set's date range and conditions. Upcoming transactions can include recurring previews that match the same include/exclude conditions and amount limits. Previews are not saved transactions and do not enter the editor's matching counters or Mass Update. The Sets list's amount summaries use saved transactions; the transaction screen's Upcoming totals also include matching previews within its selected dates.

This is useful when you want to:
- Review the matching transactions in detail
- Edit individual transactions
- Verify that the set is catching the right data

### Analytics for a Set

Choose **Analytics** from the set’s menu to open its matching transactions for the set’s resolved period. Each drill-down keeps the set conditions: `Vacation › Groceries › Store A` shows only grocery transactions at Store A that belong to Vacation. Changing the analytics dates reloads that selection without changing the saved set itself.

Use the **Transactions** option inside analytics to inspect the matching purchases, or return through the compact breadcrumbs below the summary. See [Analytics & Reports](https://budgetum.app/help/analytics) for breakdown availability, comparisons, and transaction grouping.

### More Menu

Tap the three-dot button, or long-press the card, to open these actions:
- **Transactions** - Opens the filtered transaction list
- **Analytics** - Opens analytics for the matching transactions
- **Mass Update** - Applies bulk changes to all matching transactions
- **Edit** - Changes the set's name, period, or conditions
- **Add to Budget** - Includes the set on Budget in every period, with no plan until you add one there. Shown when the set is not already on Budget. Requires Pro; otherwise the upgrade screen opens. If you upgrade and return, the set is included
- **Unlink from Budget** - Replaces **Add to Budget** when the set is already on Budget. Removes it from Budget in every period without deleting the set or its saved plans. Available even without Pro
- **Delete** - Removes the saved set after confirmation

Deleting a set does **not** delete the transactions inside it. It only removes the saved filter.

### When an item used by a set is deleted

If you delete a tag, contact, category, section, or account that a set's conditions use, the set is updated automatically, without a separate warning. The deleted item is removed from those conditions. If it was the only item in a condition, that condition is removed. If the condition was the only one in its group, the group is removed too. The set then matches using its remaining conditions, so its transaction count and totals can change. For example, a set with only **Tag: Trip** matches all transactions (within its period and amount range) after the Trip tag is deleted. A set with **has all of Trip, Hotel** becomes **has all of Hotel**. Removing an item from an exclude condition does not change which transactions the set shows. Merging keeps sets pointing at the merged item instead.

---

## Creating or Editing a Set

When you create or edit a set, the screen has Include and Exclude tabs in the top bar. The rest of the screen scrolls together: name, optional period, optional amount range, then the conditions for the selected tab.

The save button is the checkmark in the top bar. The **⋮** menu beside it opens **Transactions**, **Analytics**, and **Mass Update** for the name, period, amount, and conditions currently on the screen, including changes that are not saved. An empty name uses the create or edit title on those screens. If the end date is before the start date, the period error appears and the screen does not open. Leaving the editor without the checkmark still discards the set. **Mass Update** still changes the matching saved transactions. Recurring previews on **Transactions → Upcoming** still follow the last saved set; a set that has never been saved shows no previews.

### Name

Every set needs a name. This is the title shown in the list.

### Period

Period is optional. If no dates are set, the editor shows a compact **Period** chip under the name, on the same row as **Amount** when that filter is also unused. Tap **Period** to add:

- **Start date**
- **End date**

Each date field has an **×**. If you clear a date and the other date is empty, the date fields hide and the **Period** chip returns. If you leave the end date empty, the set continues up to **Now**. If both dates are empty, the set can match transactions across all available time.

### Amount range

Amount is also optional and applies to the whole set, not to a single group. If no amount range is set, the editor shows a compact **Amount** chip next to **Period**. Tap it to add **Minimum amount** and **Maximum amount**.

The collapsed amount line shows both limits with **AND** between them, such as `>= 5  AND  <= 6`. Use **×** to remove the amount filter even if you have not entered values yet. The **Amount** chip then returns.

### Include Tab

The Include tab defines what should match.

Conditions are grouped:
- Conditions in the same group all have to match (**AND**)
- Separate groups are alternatives (**OR**)

A new set starts with one group. Use **Add condition** inside a group to add another rule to that group. Use **Add group** to start an alternative combination. A grey **OR** divider appears between groups. Each group has an **×** on the Add condition row so you can remove it, including when there is only one group. Removing the last group leaves no include conditions, so the set can match any transaction in the period and amount range that is not excluded.

Dates and the amount range stay shared constraints above the groups. They apply to the whole set, not to a single group. They are not listed in **Add condition**.

Existing sets that used **Any (OR)** keep the same results: each of those conditions becomes its own group.

The Include tab also shows a running count of the **final matching result**: transactions that satisfy any include group, the shared dates and amount range, and are not removed by Exclude. Each condition tile shows its own count instead, so you can tell a single rule apart from that combined result. The Add condition row also shows how many transactions match that group alone.

### Exclude Tab

The Exclude tab removes transactions from the result.

A transaction is removed if it matches **any** exclusion. Use this when you want a broad include rule but need to subtract certain categories, contacts, tags, accounts, or other values.

The Exclude tab count shows how many transactions match at least one exclusion in the chosen dates. Those transactions are the ones subtracted from the Include result.

---

## Available Conditions

You can add conditions for:
- **Categories**
- **Sections**
- **Contacts**
- **Tags**
- **Accounts**
- **Descriptions**
- **Category types**
- **Contact types**

The **amount range** is added with the **Amount** chip, not from **Add condition**.

Already used fields stay available in **Add condition**. Each time you add the same field, it becomes a separate condition. For example, in the same group, one Tags condition can require any of `#gift` or `#birthday`, and another Tags condition can require a name that starts with `alcohol/`. Both must match. Put those conditions in different groups if either combination should be enough.

Each condition tile keeps the compact outlined field, floating label, icon, count, and × button. The floating label includes a short matching summary, such as **Tags · All** or **Descriptions · Starts with**. Long summaries are shortened so they still fit small screens.

Matching options are chosen inside the selector for that condition. Tap the condition tile to open it, then tap an outlined dropdown at the top to choose a matching option. Each dropdown shows only the current choice until opened. Tag dropdowns sit side by side when the translated labels and text size fit; they stack on narrower screens or with larger text. Other fields have one matching dropdown. The dropdowns, selected values, and text input share a compact form card with aligned edges. That card stays at the top of the screen, so the selected chips stay visible. Available values appear in a separate list below that scrolls on its own. The form stays put when the keyboard is open.

Changes apply to the condition as you select options or values. Use Back to return to the Set editor, then use its top-right checkmark to save the Set.

### Tags

Tag conditions have two matching choices:
- **Combine values:** **Any**, **All**, or **None**
- **Match names:** **Exactly**, **Starts with**, **Ends with**, or **Contains**

**Exactly** uses the existing tag checklist. For a name pattern, choose **Starts with**, **Ends with**, or **Contains**, type in **Tag name pattern**, then tap the **+** button beside the input or submit from the keyboard to add it. Selected patterns appear above the input. Patterns also apply to tags you create later.
